sentences.zh: 楊佐，字公儀，本唐靖恭諸楊後，至佐，家於宣。

translations.literal: Yang Zuo, style name Gongyi, originally a descendant of the Jinggong branch of the Yang clan of Tang; by Zuo's time the family had settled in Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zuo, courtesy name Gongyi, was descended from the Jinggong line of the Tang Yang clan; by his generation the family had made its home in Xuan.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，為陵州推官。

translations.literal: When he attained the jinshi degree, he became judicial assistant in Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he served as judicial assistant in Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州有鹽井深五十丈，皆石也，底用柏木為幹，上出井口，垂綆而下，方能及水。

translations.literal: The prefecture had a salt well fifty zhang deep, all stone; at the bottom cypress was used as a shaft lining, extending above the mouth of the well, with ropes let down before one could reach the water.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had a salt well fifty zhang deep, cut entirely through rock. At the bottom a cypress-wood lining formed the shaft, rising above the mouth; only by lowering ropes could workers reach the water.

sentences.zh: 歲久幹摧敗，欲易之，而陰氣騰上，入者輒死；

translations.literal: After many years the lining decayed and they wished to replace it, but malign vapors rose upward and anyone who entered died at once;
translations.idiomatic: After many years the lining rotted away and they tried to replace it, but noxious vapors welled up from below and anyone who went down died on the spot;

sentences.zh: 惟天有雨，則氣隨以下，稍能施工，晴則亟止。

translations.literal: Only when heaven sent rain did the vapors descend with it so that work could proceed a little; when it cleared they had to stop immediately.
translations.idiomatic: only when it rained would the vapors sink with the moisture so that a little work could be done; as soon as the sky cleared they had to stop at once.

sentences.zh: 佐教工人以木盤貯水，穴竅灑之，如雨滴然，謂之「雨盤」。

translations.literal: Zuo taught the workers to store water in wooden trays and sprinkle it through holes like raindrops, calling this a "rain tray."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo taught the workers to hold water in wooden trays and sprinkle it through holes like falling rain, a device they called the "rain tray."

sentences.zh: 如是累月，井幹一新，利復其舊。

translations.literal: Thus for many months they worked until the well shaft was entirely renewed and its benefit restored to what it had been.
translations.idiomatic: In this way, over many months, they renewed the shaft completely and restored the well to its former yield.

sentences.zh: 累遷河陰發運判官，幹當河渠司。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to transport commissioner-assessor at Heyin and superintendent of the Office for Rivers and Canals.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to become transport commissioner-assessor at Heyin and superintendent of the Office for Rivers and Canals.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，汴水殺溢不常，漕舟不能屬。

translations.literal: In the Huangyou era the Bian River's flow was irregular and flooding uncertain, and grain-transport boats could not link up.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangyou period the Bian River's current ran erratically and floods were unpredictable, so grain barges could not be chained in convoy.

sentences.zh: 佐度地鑿瀆以通河流，於是置都水監，命佐以鹽鐵判官同判。

translations.literal: Zuo surveyed the terrain and cut channels to connect the river's flow; the Directorate-General of Water Control was then established, and Zuo was ordered to serve as associate director while holding the post of salt and iron commissioner-assessor.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo surveyed the ground and cut canals to link the river's course; the Directorate-General of Water Control was then created, and Zuo was appointed its associate director while retaining his post as salt-and-iron commissioner-assessor.

sentences.zh: 京城地勢南下，涉夏秋則苦霖潦，佐開永通河，疏溝澮出野外，自是水患息。

translations.literal: The capital's terrain sloped southward and through summer and autumn suffered from heavy rains and flooding; Zuo opened the Yongtong River and dredged ditches and canals out beyond the suburbs, and thereafter water disasters ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The capital sloped southward, and through summer and autumn it suffered from torrential rains and flooding. Zuo opened the Yongtong River and dredged channels out into the countryside, and from then on the water troubles subsided.

sentences.zh: 又議治孟陽河，議者謂不便。

translations.literal: He also proposed regulating the Mengyang River, but critics said it was impractical.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed restoring the Mengyang River, but critics argued that the project was impractical.

sentences.zh: 佐言：「國初歲轉京東粟數十萬，今所致亡幾，儻不浚復舊跡，後將廢矣。」

translations.literal: Zuo said: "At the founding of the dynasty several hundred thousand piculs of grain were transported annually from Jingdong; now almost none arrives. If we do not dredge and restore the old route, it will later be abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo said, "In the early dynasty several hundred thousand piculs of grain were shipped each year from Jingdong; today almost nothing gets through. If we do not dredge and reopen the old channel, the route will be lost for good."

sentences.zh: 乃從其策。

translations.literal: and his plan was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: His plan was adopted.

sentences.zh: 出為江、淮發運使。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as transport commissioner for the Yangzi and Huai regions.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as transport commissioner for the Yangzi and Huai circuits.

sentences.zh: 孟陽之役，調民七、八千，夷丘墓百數，怨聲盈塞。

translations.literal: For the Mengyang project seven or eight thousand commoners were conscripted and several hundred tombs were leveled, and complaints filled the air.
translations.idiomatic: The Mengyang project conscripted seven or eight thousand laborers and leveled several hundred tombs; grievances filled the land.

sentences.zh: 詔開封鞫治，官吏獨舍佐不問。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Kaifeng to investigate and punish; of the officials only Zuo was spared inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed Kaifeng to investigate and punish those responsible; of all the officials involved, only Zuo was left untouched.

sentences.zh: 糾察刑獄劉敞請加貶黜，不聽。

translations.literal: Liu Chang, the inspector of penal affairs, requested that he receive additional demotion, but this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang, the inspector of penal affairs, asked that Zuo be further demoted, but the court did not agree.

sentences.zh: 召為鹽鐵副使，拜天章閣待制，復判都水，知審官院，權發遣開封府。

translations.literal: He was recalled as vice commissioner of salt and iron, appointed Hanlin academician-attendant at the Tianzhang Pavilion, again served as associate director of water control, directed the Office for Examination of Officials, and was temporarily charged with dispatching Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice commissioner of salt and iron, made Hanlin academician-attendant at the Tianzhang Pavilion, again served as associate director of the Directorate of Water Control, directed the Office for Examination of Officials, and was temporarily assigned to dispatch affairs for Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘗使契丹，虜饋以方物，書獨稱名。

translations.literal: Once when sent as envoy to the Khitan, the barbarians presented local products; on the documents only personal names were written.
translations.idiomatic: On one mission to the Khitan, the Liao presented local products, but the accompanying documents listed only personal names.

sentences.zh: 英宗升遐，奉遺留物再往使，卒於道，年六十一。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong passed away he was sent again to deliver the bequest gifts and died on the road, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong died, he was sent again to deliver the bequest gifts and died on the journey, aged sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 詔護喪歸，賻以黃金，恤其家。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his coffin escorted home, bestowed gold as funeral gifts, and showed favor to his family.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his coffin escorted home, granted gold as funeral compensation, and extended relief to his family.

sentences.zh: 李兌，字子西，許州臨潁人。

translations.literal: Li Dui, style name Zixi, was a native of Linjing in Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dui, courtesy name Zixi, was a native of Linjing in Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，由屯田員外郎為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: After passing the jinshi examination he rose from outer-section vice director of the Directorate of Agriculture to serving censor in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he rose from outer-section vice director of the Directorate of Agriculture to palace censor.

sentences.zh: 按齊州叛卒，獄成，有欲夜篡囚者，兌以便宜斬之，人服其略。

translations.literal: Investigating mutinous soldiers in Qi Prefecture, when the case was concluded someone meant to rescue prisoners by night; Dui had him summarily beheaded on his own authority, and people admired his decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: While investigating mutinous soldiers in Qi Prefecture, when the case was closed someone plotted a nighttime rescue of the prisoners; Dui had him summarily executed on his own authority, and people admired his decisiveness.

sentences.zh: 張堯佐判河陽，兌言堯佐素無行能，不宜以戚里故用。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yaozhuo was assigned to Heyang, Dui said Yaozhuo had long lacked conduct and ability and should not be employed because of imperial kinship.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yaozhuo was assigned to Heyang, Dui argued that Yaozhuo had long lacked both character and competence and should not be appointed merely because he was an imperial in-law.

sentences.zh: 改同知諫院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be associate director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as associate director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 狄青宣撫廣西，入內都知任守忠為副，兌言以宦者觀軍容，致主將掣肘，非計，仁宗為罷守忠。

translations.literal: When Di Qing was military commissioner for Guangxi, the Inner Palace Director Ren Shouzhong was made his deputy; Dui said that having a eunuch observe military affairs would hamper the chief commander and was no good plan, and Renzong dismissed Shouzhong for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: When Di Qing was military commissioner for Guangxi, the Inner Palace Director Ren Shouzhong was made his deputy. Dui argued that placing a eunuch over military affairs would hamstring the chief commander and was a poor policy; Emperor Renzong removed Shouzhong on that account.

sentences.zh: 太常新樂成，王拱辰以為十二鍾磬一以黃鍾為律，與古異，胡瑗及阮逸亦言聲不能諧。

translations.literal: When the new music of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was completed, Wang Gongchen held that in the twelve bells and chime-stones the yellow bell served alone as the pitch standard, differing from antiquity; Hu Yuan and Ruan Yi also said the tones could not harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: When the Court of Imperial Sacrifices completed its new music, Wang Gongchen argued that all twelve bells and chime-stones were tuned to the yellow bell alone, diverging from ancient practice; Hu Yuan and Ruan Yi also said the tones could not be brought into harmony.

sentences.zh: 詔近臣集議，久而不決。

translations.literal: An edict summoned nearby ministers to deliberate together; for a long time no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered senior officials to meet and deliberate, but for a long time no decision could be reached.

sentences.zh: 兌言：「樂之道，廣大微妙，非知音入神，詎容輕議。

translations.literal: Dui said: "The way of music is vast and subtle; unless one has entered the spirit through true understanding of tone, how can it be lightly debated?
translations.idiomatic: Dui said, "The art of music is vast and subtle; unless one has attained true understanding and entered its spirit, how can it be debated lightly?

sentences.zh: 願參新舊，但取諧和近雅者，合而用之。」

translations.literal: I wish to compare the new and old and simply select what is harmonious and close to elegance, combining them for use."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the new and old be compared, and only what is harmonious and close to elegance be selected and used together."

sentences.zh: 進侍御史知雜事，擢天章閣待制、知諫院。

translations.literal: He was promoted to chief supervising censor and elevated to Hanlin academician-attendant at the Tianzhang Pavilion and director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief supervising censor and elevated to Hanlin academician-attendant at the Tianzhang Pavilion and director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 轉運使制祿與郡守殊，時有用彈劾奪節及老疾請郡者，一切得仍奉稍。

translations.literal: The salary regulations for transport commissioners differed from those of prefects; at the time those who lost their ceremonial baton through impeachment or requested a prefecture due to age and illness all still received their former stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioners were paid on a different scale from prefects; at the time, officials who lost their ceremonial baton through impeachment or sought a prefectural post because of age or illness still received their former stipends in full.

sentences.zh: 兌言非所以勸沮，乃詔悉依所居官格。

translations.literal: Dui said this was not the way to encourage and restrain, and an edict ordered that all follow the rank scale of the office they actually held.
translations.idiomatic: Dui argued that this was no way to reward merit or deter misconduct, and an edict ordered that all salaries follow the rank scale of the office actually held.

sentences.zh: 兌在言職十年，凡所論諫，不自表襮，故鮮傳世。

translations.literal: Dui held remonstrance office for ten years; everything he remonstrated about he did not trumpet himself, so little has been transmitted to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Dui held remonstrance office for ten years; because he never publicized his own memorials and remonstrances, few of them have been handed down.

sentences.zh: 出知杭州，帝書「安民」二字以寵。

translations.literal: Sent out as prefect of Hangzhou, the emperor wrote the two characters "Pacify the People" to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as prefect of Hangzhou, the emperor honored him by inscribing the two characters "Pacify the People."

sentences.zh: 徙越州，加龍圖閣直學士、知廣州，南人謂自劉氏納土後，獨兌著清節。

translations.literal: Transferred to Yue Prefecture, he was given the additional title of academician-expositor at the Longtu Pavilion and made prefect of Guangzhou; southerners said that since the Liu clan submitted their territory, only Dui had maintained incorrupt integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Yue Prefecture, he was given the additional title of academician-expositor at the Longtu Pavilion and appointed prefect of Guangzhou; southerners said that since the Liu clan surrendered their territory, Dui alone had maintained an incorruptible reputation.

sentences.zh: 還知河陽，帝又寵以詩。

translations.literal: Returning as prefect of Heyang, the emperor again honored him with a poem.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to serve as prefect of Heyang, the emperor again honored him with a poem.

sentences.zh: 徙鄧州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 富人榜僕死，繫頸投井中而以縊為解。

translations.literal: A rich man posted notice that his servant had died, strangling his neck and throwing him in a well while claiming hanging as the explanation.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy man posted notice that his servant had died by hanging, but had in fact strangled him and thrown the body into a well.

sentences.zh: 兌曰：「既赴井，復自縊，有是理乎？

translations.literal: Dui said: "Having gone into a well, then hanging oneself afterward—is there such logic?
translations.idiomatic: Dui said, "Having gone into a well, could he then have hanged himself? Does that make any sense?

sentences.zh: 必吏受賕教之爾。」

translations.literal: It must be that clerks took bribes and instructed him."
translations.idiomatic: The clerks must have taken bribes and coached him in this story."

sentences.zh: 訊之果然。

translations.literal: On interrogation this proved true.
translations.idiomatic: On interrogation, this proved exactly true.

sentences.zh: 兌歷守名郡，為政簡嚴，老益精明。

translations.literal: Dui successively governed famous prefectures, his administration simple and stern, and in old age he grew keener still.
translations.idiomatic: Dui successively governed renowned prefectures, administering them with simplicity and severity; in old age he grew keener still.

sentences.zh: 自鄧歸，泊然無仕宦意。

translations.literal: Returning from Deng, he was tranquil and had no mind for official career.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from Deng, he was at peace and had no further appetite for office.

sentences.zh: 對便殿，力丐退，英宗命無拜，以為集賢院學士、判西京御史臺。

translations.literal: At audience in the side hall he strongly begged to retire; Emperor Yingzong ordered that he need not bow and made him academician of the Hall of Assembled Literati and judge of the Western Capital Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: At audience in the side hall he pressed hard to retire; Emperor Yingzong excused him from bowing and appointed him academician of the Hall of Assembled Literati and judge of the Western Capital Censorate.

sentences.zh: 積官尚書右丞，轉工部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: Accumulating offices to vice director of the right in the Ministry of Revenue, he transferred to minister of works and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Rising through the ranks to vice director of the right in the Ministry of Revenue, he was transferred to minister of works and retired.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十六，諡曰「莊」。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-six; his posthumous title was "Zhuang."
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-six; his posthumous title was "Zhuang."

sentences.zh: 從弟先。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Xian.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Xian.

sentences.zh: 從弟 先

translations.literal: Younger cousin: Xian
translations.idiomatic: Younger cousin: Xian

sentences.zh: 先，字淵宗，起進士，為虔州觀察推官，攝吉州永新令。

translations.literal: Xian, style name Yuanzong, rose through the jinshi to be judicial assistant under the surveillance commissioner of Gan Prefecture and acted as magistrate of Yongxin in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, courtesy name Yuanzong, passed the jinshi examination and served as judicial assistant under the surveillance commissioner of Gan Prefecture, acting as magistrate of Yongxin in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兩州俗尚訟，先為辨枉直，皆得其平。

translations.literal: Both prefectures' custom favored litigation; Xian distinguished wrong from right and in every case achieved fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Both prefectures were prone to litigation; Xian distinguished right from wrong and in every case achieved a fair outcome.

sentences.zh: 知信州、南安軍，撫楚州，歷利、梓、江東、淮南轉運使。

translations.literal: He was prefect of Xin Prefecture and military commissioner of Nan'an, pacification commissioner of Chu Prefecture, and successively transport commissioner of Li, Zi, Jiangdong, and Huainan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Xin Prefecture and military commissioner of Nan'an, as pacification commissioner of Chu Prefecture, and successively as transport commissioner of the Li, Zi, Jiangdong, and Huainan circuits.

sentences.zh: 壽春民陳氏施僧田，其後貧弱，往丐食僧所而僧逐之，取僧園中筍，遂執以為盜。

translations.literal: A Chen family of Shouchun had donated fields to monks; later, impoverished, they went to beg food at the monastery and the monks drove them off; they took bamboo shoots from the monks' garden and were seized as thieves.
translations.idiomatic: A Chen family of Shouchun had once donated fields to a monastery; later, reduced to poverty, they went to beg food there and were driven away. They took bamboo shoots from the monastery garden and were arrested as thieves.

sentences.zh: 先詰其由，奪田之半以還之。

translations.literal: Xian examined the cause and took back half the fields to return to them.
translations.idiomatic: Xian investigated the matter and confiscated half the donated fields to return to the family.

sentences.zh: 所至治官如家，人目以俚語：在信為「錯安頭」，謂其無貌而有材也；

translations.literal: Wherever he went he governed his office like his household; people marked him with slang: in Xin he was "Misplaced Head," meaning he lacked presence but had talent;
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he ran his office as he would his own household. People nicknamed him in local slang: in Xin he was called "Misplaced Head," meaning he lacked imposing looks but possessed real ability;

sentences.zh: 在楚為「照天燭」，稱其明也。

translations.literal: in Chu he was "Candle Illuminating Heaven," praising his clarity.
translations.idiomatic: in Chu he was called "Candle Illuminating Heaven," praising his clarity of judgment.

sentences.zh: 楚有民迫於輸賦，殺牛鬻之。

translations.literal: In Chu a commoner, pressed by tax delivery, slaughtered an ox and sold it.
translations.idiomatic: In Chu a commoner, hard pressed to meet his tax quota, slaughtered an ox and sold the meat.

sentences.zh: 里胥白於官，先愍焉，但令與杖。

translations.literal: The village clerk reported to the authorities; Xian pitied him and only ordered beating with the rod.
translations.idiomatic: The village clerk reported the case to the authorities; Xian took pity on the man and ordered only a beating with the rod.

sentences.zh: 通判孫龍舒以為徒刑，毀其桉。

translations.literal: The vice-prefect Sun Longshu treated it as penal servitude and destroyed the case file.
translations.idiomatic: The vice-prefect Sun Longshu reclassified the offense as penal servitude and destroyed the case file.

sentences.zh: 明日龍舒來，先引囚曰：「汝罪應杖，以通判貸汝矣。」

translations.literal: The next day when Longshu came, Xian brought out the prisoner and said: "Your crime warrants the rod; the vice-prefect has spared you."
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when Longshu arrived, Xian brought out the prisoner and said, "Your crime warrants the rod, but the vice-prefect has spared you.

sentences.zh: 遣之出。

translations.literal: He sent him out.
translations.idiomatic: He sent him away.

sentences.zh: 積官至秘書監致仕。

translations.literal: Accumulating offices to director of the Palace Library, he retired.
translations.idiomatic: Rising through the ranks to director of the Palace Library, he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 兄兌尚無恙，事之彌篤。

translations.literal: His elder cousin Dui was still well; he served him with growing devotion.
translations.idiomatic: His elder cousin Dui was still living; Xian attended him with ever greater devotion.

sentences.zh: 以子敘封，得太中大夫，閑居一紀卒，年八十三。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed by his son's merit, he attained Grand Master of Palace Attendance, lived in retirement for twelve years and died, aged eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Ennobled through his son's rank, he received the title Grand Master of Palace Attendance, lived in retirement for twelve years, and died at eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 子庭玉，年六十即棄官歸養。

translations.literal: His son Tingyu at age sixty immediately left office to return home and support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tingyu, at the age of sixty, immediately resigned office to return home and care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 人賢其家法云。

translations.literal: People praised their family regulations.
translations.idiomatic: People praised the family's standards of conduct.

sentences.zh: 沈立，字立之，歷陽人。

translations.literal: Shen Li, style name Lizhi, was a native of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li, courtesy name Lizhi, was a native of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，簽書益州判官，提舉商胡埽。

translations.literal: Recommended as jinshi, he served as signing clerk and prefectural aide in Yi Prefecture and as supervisor of the Shanghu embankment.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he served as signing clerk and prefectural aide in Yi Prefecture and as supervisor of the Shanghu embankment.

sentences.zh: 采摭大河事跡、古今利病，為書曰《河防通議》，治河者悉守為法。

translations.literal: He collected records of Great River affairs and benefits and harms ancient and modern, composing a book called Comprehensive Discussion on River Defense; all who managed rivers adhered to it as law.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered records of Yellow River works and the benefits and failures of past and present policy, and compiled a book entitled Comprehensive Discussion on River Defense, which all river administrators thereafter treated as their standard.

sentences.zh: 遷兩浙轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to transport commissioner of the Two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to transport commissioner of the Two Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 蘇、湖水，民艱食，縣戒強豪民發粟以振，立亟命還之，而勸使自稱貸，須歲稔，官為責償。

translations.literal: In Su and Hu the waters rose and the people had difficulty obtaining food; the counties warned powerful families to release grain for relief; Li immediately ordered it returned and instead urged them to lend under their own names, with repayment to be guaranteed by the government when the harvest was good.
translations.idiomatic: When floods struck Su and Hu and the people faced food shortages, the counties ordered powerful families to release grain for relief. Li immediately ordered the grain returned and instead urged the wealthy to lend under their own names, with the government guaranteeing repayment once the harvest came in.

sentences.zh: 茶禁害民，山場、榷場多在部內，歲抵罪者輒數萬，而官僅得錢四萬。

translations.literal: The tea monopoly harmed the people; mountain depots and monopoly markets were mostly within his jurisdiction, and each year those punished numbered in the tens of thousands while the government received only forty thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: The tea monopoly oppressed the people; mountain depots and monopoly markets lay mostly within his jurisdiction, and each year tens of thousands were punished while the government collected only forty thousand in cash.

sentences.zh: 立著《茶法要覽》，乞行通商法，三司使張方平上其議。

translations.literal: Li authored Essentials of the Tea Law and petitioned to implement free trade in tea; the finance commissioner Zhang Fangping presented his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Li wrote Essentials of the Tea Law and petitioned to allow free trade in tea; the finance commissioner Zhang Fangping submitted his proposal to the throne.

sentences.zh: 後罷榷法，如所請；

translations.literal: Later the monopoly was abolished as he had requested;
translations.idiomatic: Later the monopoly was abolished, as he had urged;

sentences.zh: 立召為戶部判官。

translations.literal: and Li was recalled as commissioner-assessor in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: and Li was recalled as commissioner-assessor in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 奉使契丹，適行冊禮，欲令從其國服，不則見於門。

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to the Khitan, it happened that investiture rites were being performed; they wished to make him adopt their country's dress, otherwise he would be received at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to the Khitan, it happened that investiture rites were under way; they demanded that he wear Liao dress, threatening otherwise to receive him only at the gate.

sentences.zh: 立折之曰：「往年北使講見儀，未嘗令北使易冠服，況門見邪？」

translations.literal: Li rebutted them: "In past years when northern envoys negotiated audience protocol, they were never required to change cap and robes; how much less audience at the gate?"
translations.idiomatic: Li rebutted them: "In past years, when northern envoys negotiated audience protocol, they were never required to change cap and robes. How much less should we accept audience at the gate?"

sentences.zh: 契丹愧而止。

translations.literal: The Khitan were ashamed and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were shamed into backing down.

sentences.zh: 遷京西北轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to northwestern capital transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to transport commissioner for the northwestern capital region.

sentences.zh: 都水方興六塔河，召與議，立請止修五股等河及漳河，分殺水勢以省役，從之。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Water was then undertaking the Six Pagodas River; he was summoned to discuss it; Li requested stopping construction of the Wugu and other rivers and the Zhang River, dividing and reducing the water's force to spare labor, and this was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Water was then pushing the Six Pagodas River project; Li was summoned to consult. He urged halting work on the Wugu and other channels and the Zhang River, dividing the current to reduce flood force and spare labor, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 加集賢修撰、知滄州，進右諫議大夫、判都水監，出為江淮發運使。

translations.literal: He was given the additional post of compiler at the Hall of Assembled Literati and made prefect of Cang Prefecture, advanced to right remonstrance grandee and associate director of the Directorate of Water, and sent out as Yangzi-Huai transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional post of compiler at the Hall of Assembled Literati and appointed prefect of Cang Prefecture, promoted to right remonstrance grandee and associate director of the Directorate of Water, then sent out as Yangzi-Huai transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 居職辦治，加賜金，數詔嘉之。

translations.literal: In office he handled matters effectively, received additional gifts of gold, and was repeatedly praised by edict.
translations.idiomatic: In office he handled affairs efficiently, received additional grants of gold, and was repeatedly commended by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 知越州、杭州、審官西院、江寧府。

translations.literal: He was prefect of Yue and Hangzhou, of the Western Hall for Examination of Officials, and of Jiangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Yue and Hangzhou, as director of the Western Hall for Examination of Officials, and as prefect of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 初，立在蜀，悉以公粟售書，積卷數萬。

translations.literal: Early on, while in Shu, Li used all official grain funds to purchase books, accumulating tens of thousands of volumes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving in Shu, Li spent all his official grain allowance on books and amassed tens of thousands of volumes.

sentences.zh: 神宗問所藏，立上其目及所著《名山水記》三百卷。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong asked about his collection; Li submitted its catalog and his own Famed Mountains and Waters in three hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong inquired about his library, Li submitted its catalog along with his own Record of Famous Mountains and Waters in three hundred juan.

sentences.zh: 徙宣州，提舉崇禧觀。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Xuan Prefecture and made supervisor of the Chongxi Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Xuan Prefecture and made supervisor of the Chongxi Abbey.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 張掞，字文裕，齊州歷城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shan, style name Wenyu, was a native of Licheng in Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shan, courtesy name Wenyu, was a native of Licheng in Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父蘊，咸平初，監淄州兵。

translations.literal: His father Yun, early in the Xianping era, supervised the troops of Zi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yun, in the early Xianping period, supervised the troops of Zi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 契丹入寇，遊騎至淄、青間，州人將棄城，蘊拔刀遮止於門，力治守備，遊騎為之引去。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded, scouting riders reached between Zi and Qing; the prefecture's people were about to abandon the city; Yun drew his sword and barred them at the gate, energetically organizing defenses, and the scouts withdrew on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded, scouting parties reached the border between Zi and Qing; the townspeople were about to abandon the city. Yun drew his sword and blocked them at the gate, threw himself into organizing the defenses, and the scouts withdrew.

sentences.zh: 郡守愧，始謀掠為己功，反陷以罪，蘊受而不校。

translations.literal: The prefect was ashamed and at first plotted to seize the credit for himself, then instead framed Yun with a crime; Yun accepted it without disputing.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect, ashamed, at first plotted to claim the credit for himself, then instead framed Yun with a crime. Yun accepted the charge without protest.

sentences.zh: 掞幼篤孝，蘊病，刲股肉以療。

translations.literal: Shan was deeply filial from youth; when Yun fell ill he cut flesh from his thigh to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: Shan was deeply filial from childhood; when Yun fell ill, he cut flesh from his own thigh to prepare a remedy.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，知益都縣。

translations.literal: Recommended as jinshi, he was magistrate of Yidu County.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he served as magistrate of Yidu County.

sentences.zh: 當督賦租，置里胥弗用，而民皆以時入。

translations.literal: When he was to supervise tax collection he set aside the village clerks and did not use them, yet the people all paid on time.
translations.idiomatic: When it came time to collect taxes, he set the village clerks aside and did not employ them, yet the people all paid on schedule.

sentences.zh: 石介獻《息民論》，請以益都為天下法。

translations.literal: Shi Jie presented On Pacifying the People and asked that Yidu be made the model for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jie submitted On Pacifying the People and asked that Yidu be made the model for the entire realm.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，時隆寒，徒跣舉柩，叩首流血，與兄揆廬墓左。

translations.literal: During mourning for his mother, in severe cold he went barefoot bearing the coffin, knocking his head until blood flowed, and with his elder brother Kui kept vigil by the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his mother, in bitter cold he went barefoot bearing the coffin, knocking his forehead until blood ran, and with his elder brother Kui kept vigil beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 明道中，京東饑，盜起，以御史中丞范諷薦，知萊州掖縣。

translations.literal: In the Mingdao era, when Jingdong suffered famine and bandits arose, on recommendation of vice censor-in-chief Fan Feng he was made magistrate of Ye County in Lai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Mingdao period, when Jingdong suffered famine and banditry broke out, on the recommendation of vice censor-in-chief Fan Feng he was appointed magistrate of Ye County in Lai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 民訴旱於州，拒之，掞自為奏聞，詔除登、萊稅。

translations.literal: The people complained of drought to the prefecture and were refused; Shan memorialized on his own account, and an edict remitted taxes in Deng and Lai.
translations.idiomatic: When the people petitioned the prefecture about drought and were turned away, Shan memorialized on his own authority; an edict followed remitting taxes in Deng and Lai.

sentences.zh: 通判永興軍，為集賢校理，四遷為龍圖閣直學士、知成德軍。

translations.literal: He served as vice prefect of Yongxing Circuit, became collator in the Hanlin Academy, and after four promotions was appointed Hanlin associate at the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Chengde Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice prefect of Yongxing Circuit, then as a Hanlin collator, and after four promotions was made Hanlin associate at the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Chengde Circuit.

sentences.zh: 宦者閻士良為鈐轄，多撓帥權，用危法中軍校，掞直之，而劾士良。

translations.literal: The eunuch Yan Shiliang served as military overseer and often interfered with the commander's authority, using harsh laws against middle-ranking military officers; Shan spoke out frankly and impeached Shiliang.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Yan Shiliang held the post of military overseer and frequently encroached on the commander's authority, applying harsh laws against mid-level officers. Shan spoke up directly and impeached Shiliang.

sentences.zh: 英宗登極，朝廷使來告，士良辭疾居家，宴客自若，奏抵其罪。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, court envoys came to announce it; Shiliang pleaded illness and stayed home, entertaining guests as usual; Shan memorialized to charge him with the offense.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, envoys arrived from court with the announcement. Shiliang pleaded illness and remained at home, entertaining guests as if nothing had happened. Shan memorialized to have him charged.

sentences.zh: 入判太常、司農寺，累官戶部侍郎致仕。

translations.literal: He entered service as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Directorate of Agriculture, rose through offices to vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Directorate of Agriculture, eventually rose to vice minister of revenue, and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 熙寧七年，卒，年八十。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xining he died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Xining era he died, at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 掞忠篤誠愨，既老益康寧。

translations.literal: Shan was loyal, sincere, and honest; as he grew old he became even more hale and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Shan was loyal, sincere, and upright; in old age he grew only more vigorous and serene.

sentences.zh: 少從劉潛、李冠遊，及其死，率里人葬之，置田贍其孥。

translations.literal: In youth he associated with Liu Qian and Li Guan; when they died he led villagers to bury them and set aside fields to support their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he kept company with Liu Qian and Li Guan. When they died, he led the villagers in burying them and endowed fields to provide for their families.

sentences.zh: 事揆如父，理家必諮而行，為鄉黨矜式。

translations.literal: He treated Kui as a father; in managing the household he always consulted before acting, and was a model for the village community.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his elder brother Kui as he would a father, and in household affairs never acted without consulting him first, becoming a model for the local community.

sentences.zh: 張燾，字景元，樞密直學士奎之子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Dao, style name Jingyuan, was the son of Hanlin academician-attendant Kui of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dao, courtesy name Jingyuan, was the son of Zhang Kui, Hanlin academician-attendant at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，通判單州。

translations.literal: Recommended as jinshi, he served as vice prefect of Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he served as vice prefect of Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州卒謀亂，期有日，燾得告者，徐詣營取首惡，置諸法。

translations.literal: Garrison soldiers plotted rebellion with a fixed date; Dao received an informer, went leisurely to the camp, seized the ringleaders, and punished them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison soldiers plotted a mutiny for a set day. Dao received a tip, went calmly to the camp, seized the ringleaders, and dealt with them under the law.

sentences.zh: 知沂、濰二州。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Yi and Wei prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Yi and Wei prefectures.

sentences.zh: 沂產布，濰產絹，而有司科賦相反，燾始革之。

translations.literal: Yi produced cloth and Wei produced silk, but the officials' tax assessments were reversed; Dao was the first to reform this.
translations.idiomatic: Yi produced cloth and Wei produced silk, yet the tax assessments imposed by officials had them reversed. Dao was the first to correct the practice.

sentences.zh: 濰多圭田，率計畝徵絹，而蠲河役，燾不肯踵例，廢法還其役，入損於舊五之四，且命吏曰：「吾知守己而已，無妨後人，汝勿著為式。」

translations.literal: Wei had many tax-exempt fields; generally silk tax was assessed by the mu while river corvée was waived. Dao refused to follow precedent, abolished the exemption and restored corvée, reducing revenue to four-fifths of the former amount, and also told his clerks: "I only know to guard my own integrity; do not hinder those who come after — you must not record this as a precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Wei had many tax-exempt estates; customarily silk was levied by the acre while river corvée was waived. Dao refused to follow suit, revoked the exemption and restored corvée duty, cutting revenue to four-fifths of what it had been. He told his staff: "I know only how to keep my own conscience clear. Do not make things harder for those who follow — do not set this down as a model."

sentences.zh: 提點河北刑獄，攝領澶州，七日而商胡決。

translations.literal: As intendant of penal affairs for Hebei, he temporarily took charge of Dan Prefecture; seven days later the Shanghu levee broke.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as intendant of penal affairs for Hebei, he was temporarily placed in charge of Dan Prefecture; seven days later the Shanghu levee burst.

sentences.zh: 燾拯溺救饑，所全活者十餘萬，猶坐免。

translations.literal: Dao rescued the drowning and relieved famine; more than a hundred thousand lives were saved, yet he was still dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Dao saved people from drowning and famine, preserving more than a hundred thousand lives, yet he was still removed from office.

sentences.zh: 數年，復提點河東、陝西、京西刑獄，為鹽鐵判官、淮南轉運使、江淮發運副使。

translations.literal: Several years later he again served as intendant of penal affairs for Hedong, Shaanxi, and Jingxi circuits, as salt and iron commissioner-assessor, Huainan transport commissioner, and vice commissioner for Yangzi-Huai grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he again served as intendant of penal affairs for Hedong, Shaanxi, and Jingxi, and also as salt and iron commissioner-assessor, Huainan transport commissioner, and vice commissioner for Yangzi-Huai grain transport.

sentences.zh: 泗州水，城且壞，燾悉力營護，詔寵其勞。

translations.literal: Si Prefecture was flooded and the walls were about to collapse; Dao exerted all effort in maintenance and repair, and an edict honored his labor.
translations.idiomatic: When Si Prefecture was inundated and its walls threatened to collapse, Dao threw all his strength into repairs. An edict commended his exertions.

sentences.zh: 入為戶部副使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as vice commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as vice commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 京師賦麴於酒，人有常籍，毋問售不售，或蹶產以償。

translations.literal: In the capital, yeast for brewing was levied on wine merchants; each person had a fixed register, regardless of whether they sold or not, and some bankrupted their estates to pay.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, brewer's yeast was taxed on wine sellers by fixed registration, whether or not they actually sold wine, and some ruined their estates trying to pay.

sentences.zh: 燾請罷歲額，嚴禁令，隨所用麴多寡以售，自是課增溢。

translations.literal: Dao requested abolishing the annual quota, tightening prohibitions, and selling yeast according to actual usage; thereafter tax revenue increased.
translations.idiomatic: Dao asked that the annual quota be abolished, enforcement tightened, and yeast sold according to actual need. Revenue thereafter rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 官修睦親宅，議取民居，燾言：「芳林園有餘地，宗室足自處，無庸起民居。」

translations.literal: The court planned to repair the Mujin Residence and proposed seizing private homes; Dao said: "There is spare land in Fanglin Garden; the imperial clan have room enough for themselves — there is no need to disturb private residences."
translations.idiomatic: When the court planned to renovate the Mujin Residence and proposed seizing private homes, Dao said: "Fanglin Garden still has unused land, and the imperial clan have ample room — there is no need to tear down people's houses."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 孝嚴殿成，請圖乾興以來文武大臣像於壁。

translations.literal: When the Xiaoyan Hall was completed, he requested that portraits of civil and military ministers since the Qianxing era be painted on the walls.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xiaoyan Hall was completed, he asked that portraits of civil and military ministers since the Qianxing reign be painted on its walls.

sentences.zh: 遷天章閣待制、陝西都轉運使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin attendant-at-large at the Tianzhang Pavilion and chief transport commissioner for Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin attendant-at-large at the Tianzhang Pavilion and appointed chief transport commissioner for Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 蒲津浮橋壞，鐵牛皆沒水中，燾以策列巨木於岸以為衡，縋石其秒，挽出之，橋復其初。

translations.literal: The floating bridge at Pujin was damaged and the iron oxen all sank in the water; Dao devised a plan of arraying huge logs on the bank as a fulcrum, suspending stones at their tips, and hauling the oxen out — the bridge was restored to its original state.
translations.idiomatic: When the floating bridge at Pujin broke and the iron oxen sank, Dao had massive logs lined up on the bank as levers, stones hung from their ends, and the oxen winched out. The bridge was restored to its former condition.

sentences.zh: 保安二土豪善騎射，為邊人所憚，故縱善馬誘使取之，而強以漢法。

translations.literal: Two local strongmen in Bao'an were skilled at horsemanship and archery and feared by border people; they deliberately let fine horses loose to entice people to take them, then coerced them under Han law.
translations.idiomatic: Two local magnates in Bao'an were expert riders and archers whom border people feared. They would deliberately release fine horses to lure men into taking them, then trap them under Han law.

sentences.zh: 燾按得其狀，俱以隸軍。

translations.literal: Dao investigated and obtained proof; both were enrolled as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Dao investigated and established the facts; both men were conscripted into the army.

sentences.zh: 加龍圖閣直學士、知成都府。

translations.literal: He was added as Hanlin associate at the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Hanlin associate at the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 蜀人苦多盜，燾嚴保伍，使不得隱，而申其捕限。

translations.literal: The people of Shu suffered from many bandits; Dao strictly enforced mutual surveillance so crimes could not be concealed, and tightened capture deadlines.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu were plagued by bandits. Dao strictly enforced the mutual-responsibility system so offenders could not be hidden, and shortened the deadlines for apprehension.

sentences.zh: 南蠻寇黎、雅，討走之，罷磨刀崖戍卒。

translations.literal: Southern barbarians raided Li and Ya; he campaigned and drove them off, then disbanded the garrison at Madao Cliff.
translations.idiomatic: When southern tribes raided Li and Ya, he drove them back and then disbanded the garrison at Madao Cliff.

sentences.zh: 改知瀛州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to govern Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 母喪服闋。

translations.literal: When the mourning period for his mother ended.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period for his mother had ended.

sentences.zh: 故事，起執政以詔，近臣以堂帖；

translations.literal: Per precedent, reappointing grand councillors after mourning was by edict, and close ministers by chancellery memo;
translations.idiomatic: By established practice, grand councillors returning from mourning were reappointed by edict, and close ministers by chancellery memo;

sentences.zh: 神宗特命賜詔。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong specially ordered an edict of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong specially issued an edict to recall him.

sentences.zh: 判太常寺，知鄧、許二州，復判太常，知通進銀臺司，提舉崇福宮，由給事中易通議大夫。

translations.literal: He served as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, prefect of Deng and Xu, again vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, director of the Office for Memorials and Documents, superintendent of Chongfu Palace, and was promoted from Supervising Censor to Grand Master of Manifest Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Deng and Xu, again as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then as director of the Office for Memorials and Documents and superintendent of Chongfu Palace, and was promoted from Supervising Censor to Grand Master of Manifest Counsel.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 燾才智敏給，常從范仲淹使河東。

translations.literal: Dao was talented, quick, and resourceful; he often accompanied Fan Zhongyan on missions to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Dao was clever and quick-witted, and often accompanied Fan Zhongyan on missions to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 至汾州，民遮道數百趨訴，仲淹以付燾，方與客弈，局未終，處決已竟。

translations.literal: At Fen Prefecture, hundreds of people blocked the road to petition; Fan Zhongyan handed them to Dao; he was in the middle of a game with a guest, and before the game ended the cases had all been decided.
translations.idiomatic: At Fen Prefecture, hundreds of people blocked the road with petitions. Fan Zhongyan turned them over to Dao, who was playing chess with a guest; before the game was finished, every case had been settled.

sentences.zh: 英宗時，三司前奏事，帝詰鑄錢本末，皆不能對，燾悉論無隱。

translations.literal: During Yingzong's reign, when officials of the Directorate of Three Departments were reporting, the emperor asked about the origins and ends of coin casting; none could answer, but Dao explained everything without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yingzong, when the Directorate of Three Departments presented its business, the emperor questioned them on the full history of coin casting. No one could answer, but Dao explained every detail without reserve.

sentences.zh: 帝是之，顧左右識其姓名，後欲以為觀察使守邊，曰：「卿家世事也。」

translations.literal: The emperor approved, told attendants to note his name; later wishing to appoint him as military commissioner to guard the frontier, he said: "Your family has long served in border affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and told his attendants to remember Dao's name. Later, intending to appoint him military commissioner to guard the frontier, he said: "Border service runs in your family."

sentences.zh: 燾對曰：「臣叔父亢有大才，臣愚不可繼。」

translations.literal: Dao replied: "My uncle Kang has great talent; I am dull and cannot succeed to the post."
translations.idiomatic: Dao replied: "My uncle Kang has far greater ability. I am too dull to follow in his footsteps."

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: And the matter stopped there.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment went no further.

sentences.zh: 俞充，字公達，明州鄞人。

translations.literal: Yu Chong, style name Gongda, was a native of Yin in Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chong, courtesy name Gongda, was a native of Yin in Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 登進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中為都水丞，提舉沿汴淤泥溉田，為上腴者八萬頃。

translations.literal: During Xining he served as vice director of water control, supervising the use of Bian River silt to irrigate fields, yielding eighty thousand qing of top-grade land.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era he served as vice director of water control, overseeing the use of Bian River silt to irrigate fields and creating eighty thousand qing of prime farmland.

sentences.zh: 檢正中書戶房，加集賢校理、淮南轉運副使，遷成都路轉運使。

translations.literal: He served as inspector-reviser in the Household Section of the Secretariat, was added as Hanlin collator and Huainan vice transport commissioner, and was promoted to Chengdu Circuit transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as inspector-reviser in the Secretariat's Household Section, was made Hanlin collator and Huainan vice transport commissioner, and was promoted to transport commissioner of Chengdu Circuit.

sentences.zh: 茂州羌寇邊，充上十策禦戎。

translations.literal: When Qiang of Maozhou raided the border, Chong submitted ten strategies for frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiang of Maozhou raided the frontier, Chong submitted ten plans for border defense.

sentences.zh: 神宗遣內侍王中正同經制，建三堡，復永康為軍，因詐殺羌眾以為中正功，與深相結，至出妻拜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong sent the eunuch Wang Zhongzheng as co-commissioner; they built three forts and restored Yongkang as a military prefecture; Chong falsely killed Qiang people to credit Zhongzheng, became deeply allied with him, and even presented his wife to bow to Zhongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong dispatched the eunuch Wang Zhongzheng as co-commissioner. They built three forts and restored Yongkang as a military prefecture. Chong staged killings of Qiang people to burnish Zhongzheng's record, formed a close alliance with him, and even had his wife pay obeisance to Zhongzheng.

sentences.zh: 中正還闕，舉充可任。

translations.literal: Zhongzheng returned to court and recommended Chong as capable.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzheng returned to court, he recommended Chong as fit for higher office.

sentences.zh: 召判都水監，進直史館。

translations.literal: Chong was summoned to serve as vice director of the Directorate of Water Control and was promoted to academician in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was summoned to serve as vice director of the Directorate of Water Control and promoted to academician in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 中書都檢正御史彭汝礪論其媚事中正，命遂寢。

translations.literal: Chief inspector-reviser and censor Peng Ruli argued that he had fawned on Zhongzheng, and the appointment was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Chief inspector-reviser and censor Peng Ruli charged that Chong had curried favor with Zhongzheng, and the appointment was shelved.

sentences.zh: 河決曹村，充往救護，還，陳河防十餘事，概論「水衡之政不修，因循苟且，浸以成習。

translations.literal: The Yellow River broke at Caocun; Chong went to rescue; on return he submitted more than ten items on river defense, broadly stating: "Water-control policy is not maintained; procrastination and slipshod work have gradually become habit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River burst at Caocun, Chong went to the scene to help. On his return he submitted more than ten proposals on river defense, arguing in general that "water-control administration has fallen into neglect; delay and shoddy work have slowly hardened into custom.

sentences.zh: 方曹村決時，兵之在役者僅十餘人，有司自取敗事，恐未可以罪歲也。」

translations.literal: When Caocun broke, soldiers on corvée numbered barely ten or more; the officials brought failure on themselves — this can hardly be blamed on the year's misfortunes."
translations.idiomatic: When Caocun broke, there were barely a dozen soldiers on corvée duty. The officials courted disaster themselves — one can hardly blame the year's ill fortune alone."

sentences.zh: 加集賢殿修撰、提舉市易，歲登課百四十萬。

translations.literal: He was added as Hanlin compiler and superintendent of the Market Monopoly; annual revenue reached 1.4 million.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Hanlin compiler and superintendent of the Market Monopoly system, and annual revenue reached 1.4 million.

sentences.zh: 故事當賜錢，充曰：「奏課，職也，願自今罷賜。」

translations.literal: Per precedent he should have received a cash reward; Chong said: "Reporting revenue is one's duty; I wish that rewards be abolished from now on."
translations.idiomatic: By custom he was due a cash reward for his performance. Chong said: "Reporting revenue is simply one's duty. I ask that such rewards be abolished from now on."

sentences.zh: 詔聽之。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted his request.

sentences.zh: 擢天章閣待制、知慶州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin attendant at the Tianzhang Pavilion and prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin attendant at the Tianzhang Pavilion and appointed prefect of Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 慶陽兵驕，小繩治輒肆悖，充嚴約束，斬妄言者五人於軍門。

translations.literal: Qingyang troops were insubordinate; even minor discipline provoked defiance; Chong imposed strict rules and beheaded five who spoke rashly at the camp gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Qingyang garrison was unruly and rebelled at the slightest correction. Chong enforced strict discipline and beheaded five men for reckless talk at the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 聞有病苦則巡撫勞餉，死不能舉者出私財以周其喪，以故莫不畏威而懷惠。

translations.literal: When he heard of illness he inspected and supplied provisions; when men died and families could not afford burial he paid from private funds — thus all feared his authority yet cherished his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned of sickness he went to comfort the men and supply them; when soldiers died and families could not afford funerals he paid from his own purse. All feared his sternness yet felt his kindness.

sentences.zh: 環州田與夏境犬牙交錯，每獲必遭掠，多棄弗理，充檄所部復以時耕植。

translations.literal: Huan Prefecture fields interlocked with Xia territory; each harvest brought raids, so many abandoned their fields; Chong ordered subordinates to resume planting on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Fields in Huan Prefecture interlocked with Xia territory, and every harvest brought raids, so many farmers had abandoned their land. Chong ordered his subordinates to restore cultivation on schedule.

sentences.zh: 慕家族山夷叛，舉戶亡入西者且三百，充遣將張守約耀兵塞上，夏人亟反之。

translations.literal: The Muzhu clan mountain Yi rebelled; nearly three hundred households fled west; Chong sent General Zhang Shouyue to display troops at the border, and the Xia quickly returned them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Muzhu clan's mountain tribes rebelled and nearly three hundred households fled west, Chong sent General Zhang Shouyue to show force on the border, and the Xia promptly returned them.

sentences.zh: 充之帥邊，實王珪薦，欲以遏司馬光之入。

translations.literal: Chong's border command was actually recommended by Wang Gui, intending to block Sima Guang's return to power.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's appointment to command the frontier had in fact been Wang Gui's recommendation, meant to keep Sima Guang from returning to court.

sentences.zh: 充亦知帝有用兵意，屢倡請西征，後言：「夏酋秉常為母梁所戕，或云雖存而囚，不得與國政。

translations.literal: Chong also knew the emperor wished to use force and repeatedly urged western campaigns; later he said: "The Xia chief Bingchang was killed by his mother Lady Liang, or some say though alive he is imprisoned and cannot conduct state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chong also knew the emperor favored military action and repeatedly urged a western campaign. Later he said: "The Xia ruler Bingchang was slain by his mother Lady Liang — or so some say; others hold that he still lives but is imprisoned and barred from governing.

sentences.zh: 其母宣淫凶恣，國人怨嗟，實為興師問罪之秋也。

translations.literal: His mother conducts herself with wanton licentiousness and cruel arrogance; the people groan with resentment — this is truly the season to raise troops and demand justice.
translations.idiomatic: She indulges in debauchery and rules with brutal arrogance, and her people groan with resentment. This is truly the moment to march and call her to account.

sentences.zh: 秉常亡，將有桀黠者起，必為吾患。

translations.literal: If Bingchang perishes, a cunning and fierce man will rise and surely become our trouble.
translations.idiomatic: If Bingchang is gone, some fierce and cunning man will rise and become a threat to us.

sentences.zh: 今師出有名，天亡其國，度如破竹之易。

translations.literal: Now our army goes forth with righteous cause; Heaven is destroying their state — victory should be as easy as splitting bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Our campaign now has just cause, and Heaven itself is destroying their state. Conquest should be as effortless as splitting bamboo.

sentences.zh: 願得乘傳入覲，面陳攻討之略。」

translations.literal: I wish to travel post-haste to court and personally present the strategy for attack."
translations.idiomatic: I ask leave to ride post-horses to court and lay out the plan of attack in person."

sentences.zh: 詔令掾屬入議，未及行，充暴卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his staff to enter for deliberation; before he could go, Chong died suddenly, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his staff to come to court for consultation, but before he could depart Chong died suddenly, at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾，字元忠，吉州人，沆之子也。

translations.literal: Liu Jin, style name Yuanzhong, was a native of Ji Prefecture and the son of Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin, courtesy name Yuanzhong, was a native of Ji Prefecture and the son of Liu Hong.

sentences.zh: 第進士，為館閣校勘。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as collator in the Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as a collator in the palace archives.

sentences.zh: 沆亡，得褒贈。

translations.literal: When Hong died, he received posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong died, Jin received posthumous honors on his father's behalf.

sentences.zh: 知制誥張瓌草詞，語涉譏貶，瑾泣涕不能食，闔門衰絰，邀宰相自言。

translations.literal: Document drafter Zhang Gui drafted the eulogy with language involving mockery and belittlement; Jin wept and could not eat, the entire household wore mourning garb, and he invited the chief councillor to explain in person.
translations.idiomatic: When document drafter Zhang Gui drafted the eulogy in language that seemed to mock and belittle his father, Jin wept until he could not eat. His whole household donned mourning dress, and he asked the chief councillor to hear him out in person.

sentences.zh: 朝廷為改書命，黜瓌為州，瑾亦坐衰服入公門罷職。

translations.literal: The court rewrote the appointment, demoted Gui to a prefecture, and Jin was also dismissed for entering official quarters while in mourning garb.
translations.idiomatic: The court revised the text, demoted Gui to a prefectural post, and dismissed Jin as well for entering the government offices while still in mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 沒喪不就官，丐守墳墓。

translations.literal: After his father's death he did not take office, begging to guard the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he refused appointment and begged only to guard the tomb.

sentences.zh: 王素為請，以伸孝子之志。

translations.literal: Wang Su petitioned on his behalf to fulfill the filial son's wish.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su interceded for him so that he might fulfill a filial son's wish.

sentences.zh: 詔復職，遷集賢校理、通判睦州，為淮南轉運副使。

translations.literal: An edict restored his office; he was promoted to Hanlin collator and vice prefect of Mu Prefecture, and served as Huainan vice transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored him to office. He was promoted to Hanlin collator and vice prefect of Mu Prefecture, and later served as Huainan vice transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 召修起居注，加史館修撰、河北轉運使，拜天章閣待制、知瀛州。

translations.literal: He was summoned to compile the Veritable Records, added as historiography compiler and Hebei transport commissioner, and appointed Hanlin attendant and prefect of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to compile the Veritable Records, made historiography compiler and Hebei transport commissioner, and appointed Hanlin attendant and prefect of Ying.

sentences.zh: 坐與世居通問，徙明州。

translations.literal: He was demoted for exchanging correspondence with Wang Shiju and transferred to Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for corresponding with Wang Shiju and transferred to Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未行，改鎮廣州。

translations.literal: Before he departed, he was reassigned to govern Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, he was reassigned to govern Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 與樞密院論戍兵不合，改虔州。

translations.literal: He disagreed with the Bureau of Military Affairs on garrison troops and was transferred to Gan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After clashing with the Bureau of Military Affairs over garrison troops, he was moved to Gan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 戰棹都監楊從先奉旨募兵不至，擅遣其子懋糾諸縣巡檢兵集郡下，瑾怒責之，遽發悖謬語，懋訴瑾於朝，遂廢於家。

translations.literal: Naval commander Yang Congxian was ordered to recruit troops but failed to arrive; he arbitrarily sent his son Mao to muster county patrol troops at the prefectural seat; Jin angrily rebuked him; Mao suddenly uttered rebellious and absurd words; Mao petitioned against Jin at court, and Jin was dismissed and lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: Naval commander Yang Congxian, ordered to raise troops, failed to report on time and on his own authority sent his son Mao to assemble county patrol forces at the prefectural seat. Jin rebuked him sharply; Mao suddenly spoke in wild and seditious terms and then accused Jin at court. Jin was dismissed and returned home.

sentences.zh: 逾年，復待制、知江州，歷福州、秦州、成德軍，卒。

translations.literal: After a year he was restored as attendant and prefect of Jiang Prefecture, served Fuzhou, Qin Prefecture, and Chengde Circuit, and died.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was restored as Hanlin attendant and prefect of Jiang Prefecture, later served Fuzhou, Qin Prefecture, and Chengde Circuit, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 瑾素有操尚，所蒞以能稱，然御下苛嚴，少縱舍，好面折人短，以故多致訾怨。

translations.literal: Jin had integrity throughout; wherever he served he was known for competence, yet he governed subordinates harshly with little leniency, liked to confront people's faults to their faces, and for this drew much criticism and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had always been a man of principle and was regarded as capable wherever he served, yet he ruled subordinates with harsh severity and little mercy, and liked to expose others' faults to their faces — for which he earned much resentment.

sentences.zh: 閻詢，字議道，鳳翔天興人。

translations.literal: Yan Xun, style name Yidao, was a native of Tianxing in Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xun, courtesy name Yidao, was a native of Tianxing in Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 少時以學問著聞，擢進士第，又中書判拔萃科。

translations.literal: Renowned for learning from youth, he passed the jinshi examination and also passed the Zhongshu exceptional-talent examination.
translations.idiomatic: Known from youth for his scholarship, he passed the jinshi examination and also won the Zhongshu exceptional-talent selection.

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書丞，為監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: He rose to secretary and served as acting investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of secretary and served as acting investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 詔治王素獄，坐有姻嫌不以聞，降監河陽酒稅，累遷為鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: Ordered to investigate Wang Su's case, for failing to report a marriage connection he was demoted to supervisor of Heyang wine tax, and eventually rose to salt and iron commissioner-assessor.
translations.idiomatic: When ordered to investigate Wang Su's case, he failed to disclose a marriage tie and was demoted to supervisor of the Heyang wine tax. He eventually rose again to salt and iron commissioner-assessor.

sentences.zh: 使契丹。

translations.literal: He was sent as envoy to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as envoy to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 詢頗諳北方疆理，時契丹在靴淀，迓者王惠導詢由松亭往，詢曰：「此松亭路也，胡不徑蔥嶺而迂枉若是，豈非誇大國地廣以相欺邪？」

translations.literal: Xun knew northern geography well; the Khitan were at Xueyan; greeter Wang Hui guided Xun by the Songting route; Xun said: "This is the Songting route — why not go directly via Congling, but make such a circuitous detour? Is this not to boast of your vast territory and deceive us?"
translations.idiomatic: Xun was well versed in northern geography. The Khitan court was at Xueyan, and the escort Wang Hui led him by way of Songting. Xun said: "This is the Songting road. Why not go straight by Congling, but take such a roundabout path? Are you not trying to impress us with how vast your realm is?"

sentences.zh: 惠慚不能對。

translations.literal: Hui was ashamed and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was abashed and had no answer.

sentences.zh: 加直龍圖閣、知梓州。

translations.literal: He was added as Hanlin associate at the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Zi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Hanlin associate at the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Zi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 徙河東轉運使，言：「三路土兵疲老者，聽其族以強壯者代。」

translations.literal: Transferred to Hedong transport commissioner, he said: "For local militia who are weary and aged on the three circuits, allow their clans to substitute strong young men."
translations.idiomatic: After he was transferred to Hedong transport commissioner, he proposed: "For aged and worn-out local militia on the three frontier circuits, let their clans replace them with stronger young men."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 進集賢殿修撰、知河中府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin compiler and prefect of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin compiler and appointed prefect of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 大河漲，壞浮橋，詢易為長橋。

translations.literal: The Yellow River rose and destroyed the floating bridge; Xun replaced it with a long bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River swelled and wrecked the floating bridge, Xun rebuilt it as a long fixed bridge.

sentences.zh: 拜天章閣待制、知廣州，不即赴，罷職知商州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin attendant and prefect of Guang Prefecture; he did not promptly report, was dismissed from that post, and made prefect of Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin attendant and prefect of Guang Prefecture, but did not report promptly and was removed from that appointment and made prefect of Shang.

sentences.zh: 神宗轉右諫議大夫，改邠、同二州，提舉上清太平宮，卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong transferred him to Right Remonstrance Officer; he served Bin and Tong prefectures, was superintendent of Shangqing Taiping Palace, and died, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong promoted him to Right Remonstrance Officer. He governed Bin and Tong prefectures, served as superintendent of Shangqing Taiping Palace, and died at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 葛宮，字公雅，江陰人。

translations.literal: Ge Gong, style name Gongya, was a native of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Gong, courtesy name Gongya, was a native of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，授忠正軍掌書記。

translations.literal: Recommended as jinshi, he was appointed recorder of Zhongzheng Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he was appointed recorder of Zhongzheng Circuit.

sentences.zh: 善屬文，上《太平雅頌》十篇，真宗嘉之，召試學士院，進兩階。

translations.literal: He was skilled at literary composition; he submitted ten scrolls of the Taiping Elegant Eulogies. Emperor Zhenzong praised him, summoned him for examination at the Hanlin Academy, and he was promoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in prose, he presented ten scrolls of the Taiping Elegant Eulogies. Emperor Zhenzong was pleased, had him examined at the Hanlin Academy, and advanced him two ranks.

sentences.zh: 又獻《寶符閣頌》，為楊億所稱。

translations.literal: He also presented the Ode to the Bao Fu Pavilion, which Yang Yi praised.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted the Ode to the Bao Fu Pavilion, which won praise from Yang Yi.

sentences.zh: 知南充縣，東川饑，民艱食，部使者檄守資、昌兩州，以惠政聞。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Nanchong County, when Eastern Chuan suffered famine and the people had difficulty obtaining food, the circuit commissioner ordered him to administer Zi and Chang prefectures; he became known for benevolent governance.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as magistrate of Nanchong County, famine struck Eastern Chuan and food grew scarce. The circuit commissioner dispatched him to hold Zi and Chang prefectures, where his humane administration won wide renown.

sentences.zh: 知南劍州。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Southern Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Southern Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 土豪彭孫聚黨數百，憑依山澤為盜，出害吏民，不可捕，宮遣沙縣尉許抗諭降之。

translations.literal: A local strongman, Peng Sun, gathered several hundred followers, relied on mountains and marshes to become bandits, went out to harm officials and people, and could not be captured. Gong sent Xu Kang, assistant magistrate of Shaxian, to persuade them to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: A local magnate named Peng Sun rallied several hundred men, made his base in the hills and marshes, and raided officials and commoners alike; no one could take him. Gong dispatched Xu Kang, assistant magistrate of Shaxian, to talk the band into surrender.

sentences.zh: 並溪山多產銅、銀，吏挾奸罔利，課歲不登，宮一變其法，歲羨餘六百萬。

translations.literal: The mountains along Bing Creek produced much copper and silver; officials used deceit to seek profit, and annual tax receipts fell short. Gong changed the method in one stroke, and each year there was a surplus of six million.
translations.idiomatic: The hills around Bing Creek were rich in copper and silver, but corrupt officials had skimmed the profits and annual levies routinely fell short. Gong overhauled the system at a stroke, and within a year the treasury showed a surplus of six million cash.

sentences.zh: 三司使聞於朝，論當賞。

translations.literal: The Director of the Three Departments reported it to court and argued that he should be rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: The fiscal commissioner reported the matter to court and argued that Gong deserved a reward.

sentences.zh: 宮曰：「天地所產，吾顧盜之，又可為功乎？」

translations.literal: Gong said, "What heaven and earth produce—how could I merely steal it? How could that count as merit?"
translations.idiomatic: Gong said, "These are gifts of heaven and earth—how could I simply plunder them and call it achievement?"

sentences.zh: 卒不言。

translations.literal: In the end he said nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he never spoke of it again.

sentences.zh: 徙知滁、秀二州，秀介江湖間，吏為關涇瀆上，以征往來，間有昏葬，趨期者多不克，宮命悉毀之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Chu and Xiu prefectures. Xiu lay between rivers and lakes; officials set up barriers on streams and canals to levy tolls on travelers. Sometimes there were burials at dusk, and many who hurried to meet deadlines could not manage it. Gong ordered all such barriers destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chu and Xiu prefectures. Xiu stood amid rivers and lakes, where officials had erected toll stations on streams and canals to tax travelers. Late burials often forced mourners to race deadlines they could not meet. Gong ordered every such barrier torn down.

sentences.zh: 積官秘書監、太子賓客。

translations.literal: Through accumulated appointments he reached Director of the Secretariat and Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: By accumulated rank he rose to Director of the Secretariat and Guest of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 治平中，轉工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Zhiping era he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiping reign he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 熙寧五年，卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xining he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of the Xining era, at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 宮性敦厚，恤錄宗黨，撫孤嫠，賴以存者甚眾。

translations.literal: Gong's nature was sincere and generous; he cared for and supported his clan, comforted orphans and widows, and very many relied on him to survive.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was warm and generous by nature. He looked after his kinsmen, supported orphans and widows, and a great many people owed their livelihood to him.

sentences.zh: 宮弟密，亦以進士為光州推官。

translations.literal: Gong's younger brother Mi also passed the jinshi examination and served as judicial assistant in Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gong's younger brother Mi also earned the jinshi degree and served as judicial assistant in Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 豪民李新殺人，嫁其罪於邑民葛華，且用華之子為證。

translations.literal: A powerful local man, Li Xin, killed someone and shifted the crime onto the townsman Ge Hua, even using Hua's son as witness.
translations.idiomatic: A local magnate named Li Xin committed murder and pinned the crime on a townsman, Ge Hua, even forcing Hua's own son to testify against him.

sentences.zh: 獄具，密得其情，出之。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, Mi learned the truth and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Once the case was closed, Mi uncovered the truth and freed Ge Hua.

sentences.zh: 法當賞，密白州使勿言。

translations.literal: By law he should have been rewarded; Mi told the prefectural commissioner not to report it.
translations.idiomatic: The law entitled him to a reward, but Mi asked the prefectural commissioner to say nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 仕至太常博士。

translations.literal: In office he reached Erudite of the Grand Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in office to Erudite of the Grand Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 天性恬靖，年五十，忽上章致仕，姻黨交止之，笑曰：「俟罪疾、老死不已而休官者，安得有餘裕哉。」

translations.literal: By nature he was tranquil and retiring. At fifty he suddenly submitted a memorial to retire. Relatives and friends tried to stop him; he smiled and said, "Those who wait until guilt, illness, or old age before leaving office—how can they have any leisure left?"
translations.idiomatic: Tranquil and retiring by nature, at fifty he suddenly petitioned to retire. Relatives and friends urged him to reconsider. He smiled and said, "Those who wait until they are guilty, sick, or dying before they quit office—what leisure will they have left then?"

sentences.zh: 即退居，號「草堂逸老」，年八十四乃終。

translations.literal: He then withdrew to private life, styled himself "Hermit Elder of the Thatched Hall," and died only at eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew at once, took the style Hermit Elder of the Thatched Hall, and did not die until he was eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 平生為詩慕李商隱，有西昆高致。

translations.literal: All his life in poetry he admired Li Shangyin and possessed the lofty spirit of the Xikun school.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote poetry all his life in admiration of Li Shangyin and achieved the refined elegance of the Xikun style.

sentences.zh: 子書思，踵登第，調建德主簿。

translations.literal: His son Shu Si followed him in passing the examinations and was assigned as chief clerk of Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shu Si followed in his footsteps, passed the examinations, and was appointed chief clerk of Jiande.

sentences.zh: 時密已老，欲迎以之官，密難之。

translations.literal: By then Mi was already old; Shu Si wished to bring him to his post, but Mi found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: By then Mi was already elderly, and Shu Si wanted to bring him along to his new post, but Mi was reluctant.

sentences.zh: 書思曰：「曾子不肯一日去親側，豈以五斗移素志哉？」

translations.literal: Shu Si said, "Zengzi would not leave his parent's side for even one day—how could five dou of salary shift a pure resolve?"
translations.idiomatic: Shu Si said, "Zengzi would not leave his parents' side for a single day—how could a petty salary change a lifelong resolve?"

sentences.zh: 遂投劾歸養十年餘。

translations.literal: He then submitted his resignation and returned home to support his father for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned his post and returned home to care for his father for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 近臣表其志行，以為泗州教授，弗就。

translations.literal: A court intimate memorialized his conduct and character, and he was appointed professor at Sizhou, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: A court intimate recommended his character and conduct, and he was offered the post of professor at Sizhou, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 密不得已，許以他日偕行，始乞監新市鎮。

translations.literal: Mi, unable to refuse further, agreed that they would travel together another day; only then did Shu Si request appointment as supervisor of Xinshi Town.
translations.idiomatic: Mi could hold out no longer and agreed they would travel together on some later day; only then did Shu Si accept appointment as supervisor of Xinshi Town.

sentences.zh: 居父喪，哀毀骨立，盛暑不釋苴麻，終禫不忍去塚舍。
