translations.literal: While observing mourning for his father, his grief wasted him until only bone remained; in the height of summer he would not remove his hemp garments, and even after the final mourning period he could not bear to leave the grave lodge.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his father he grieved until he was skin and bone; even in midsummer he would not lay aside his mourning garb, and after the final rites he still could not bring himself to leave the grave-side lodge.

sentences.zh: 累年，乃出仕，歷封丘主簿、漣水。

translations.literal: After several years he finally returned to office, serving successively as chief clerk of Fengqiu and of Lianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Only after several years did he return to office, serving in turn as chief clerk of Fengqiu and of Lianshui.

sentences.zh: 時兄書元為望江令，同隸淮南監司，有舍兄而薦己者，移書乞改薦兄，不許，則封檄還之。

translations.literal: At the time his elder brother Shu Yuan was magistrate of Wangjiang; both were under the Huainan supervisory commissioner. When someone passed over his brother to recommend him instead, he wrote asking that the recommendation be changed to his brother. When this was refused, he sealed the dispatch and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shu Yuan was then magistrate of Wangjiang, and both brothers served under the same Huainan supervisory commissioner. When someone passed over Shu Yuan to recommend Shu Si instead, he wrote asking that the recommendation be redirected to his brother. When that was refused, he sealed the commission and sent it back unopened.

sentences.zh: 其篤行類皆若此。

translations.literal: His earnest conduct was in every respect of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His steadfast integrity was everywhere of this sort.

sentences.zh: 仕至朝奉郎，亦告老，父子歸休皆不待年。

translations.literal: In office he reached Court Gentleman for Attending; he too petitioned to retire, and father and son both withdrew from service before the usual age.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Court Gentleman for Attending and likewise petitioned to retire; both father and son left office before the customary age.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三，特諡曰「清孝」。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-three, and was specially given the posthumous title Qingxiao.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-three and was posthumously granted the title Qingxiao, "Pure and Filial."

sentences.zh: 子勝仲，孫立方，皆以學業至侍從，世為儒家。

translations.literal: His son Shengzhong and grandson Lifang both, through scholarship, reached attendant-in-waiting rank; for generations the family were Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shengzhong and grandson Lifang both rose through learning to become palace attendants; for generations the Ge were a scholar-official family.

sentences.zh: 勝仲自有傳。

translations.literal: Shengzhong has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzhong has a separate biography of his own.

sentences.zh: 論曰：佐、立擅水衡之政，為時所稱。

translations.literal: The discussion says: Zuo and Li excelled in fiscal administration and were praised by their age.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Zuo and Li distinguished themselves in fiscal administration and won praise in their own day.

sentences.zh: 兌居官論諫，無所表襮，先克承之。

translations.literal: Dui, in office, remonstrated and counseled without displaying himself; earlier men had inherited this quality.
translations.idiomatic: Dui counseled and remonstrated in office without parading his virtue; earlier generations had already embodied that same restraint.

sentences.zh: 掞之孝，燾之智，瑾之苛嚴，詢之辭令，皆著一時，自致顯官。

translations.literal: Shan's filial piety, Dao's wisdom, Jin's harsh severity, and Xun's eloquence all stood out in their time, and each rose by his own efforts to high office.
translations.idiomatic: Shan's filial devotion, Dao's shrewdness, Jin's harsh severity, and Xun's eloquence each made its mark in the age, and each won high office through his own merits.

sentences.zh: 俞充制軍禁暴，足為能臣，而希時相之意，倡請西征，使其不死，邊陲之禍，其可既乎？

translations.literal: Yu Chong controlled the army and forbade violence—enough to count as a capable minister—yet he courted the chief minister's favor and advocated a western campaign. Had he not died, could the border calamities have ever ended?
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chong kept the army in order and checked violence—he might well have been counted a capable minister—yet he curried favor with the chief minister and urged a western expedition. Had he lived, would the disasters on the frontier ever have ceased?

sentences.zh: 葛氏自宮以下，簪纓相繼，盛哉！

translations.literal: From Gong downward, the Ge clan produced official after official in succession—how flourishing!
translations.idiomatic: From Gong's generation onward, the Ge clan produced one capped and girdled official after another—what a flourishing house!

sentences.zh: 張田，字公載，澶淵人。

translations.literal: Zhang Tian, style name Gongzai, was a native of Chanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tian, courtesy name Gongzai, was a native of Chanyuan.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，知應天府司錄。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as registrar of Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he served as registrar of Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修薦其才，通判廣信軍。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu recommended his talent, and he became vice prefect of Guangxin Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu recommended his ability, and he was appointed vice prefect of Guangxin Circuit.

sentences.zh: 夏竦、楊懷敏建策增七郡塘水，詔通判集議，田曰：「此非禦敵策也，壞良田，浸塚墓，民被其患，不為便。」

translations.literal: Xia Song and Yang Huaimin proposed expanding pond water defenses in seven prefectures. An edict ordered the vice prefect to convene discussion. Tian said, "This is no strategy for repelling the enemy. It ruins good farmland, floods graves, and the people suffer from it—it is no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Xia Song and Yang Huaimin proposed enlarging the pond-water defenses of seven prefectures. The throne ordered the vice prefect to convene a discussion. Tian said, "This is no way to repel an enemy. It will ruin fertile fields, flood graves, and bring misery to the people—it is no improvement at all."

sentences.zh: 因奏疏極論，謫監郢州稅。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial arguing forcefully and was demoted to supervisor of the Yingzhou tax office.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial arguing the point at length and was demoted to supervisor of the Yingzhou tax office.

sentences.zh: 久之，通判冀州。

translations.literal: After a long while he became vice prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed vice prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 內侍張宗禮使經郡，酣酒自恣，守貳無敢白者，田發其事，詔配西陵灑掃。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Zhang Zongli passed through the prefecture on mission, drank heavily and indulged himself at will, and neither the prefect nor the vice prefect dared report it. Tian exposed the matter; an edict ordered Zhang assigned to menial labor at Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Zhang Zongli passed through the prefecture on imperial business, drank freely, and did as he pleased, yet neither the prefect nor his deputy dared report him. Tian exposed the affair, and an edict assigned Zhang to menial labor at Xiling.

sentences.zh: 攝度支判官。

translations.literal: He served in an acting capacity as revenue-section judge.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting revenue-section judge.

sentences.zh: 祫享太廟，又請自執政下差減賚費，唐介論其虧損上恩，出知蘄州。

translations.literal: At the winter ancestral sacrifice in the Imperial Temple, he again requested that gift expenditures be reduced from the chief administrators downward. Tang Jie argued that this diminished imperial grace, and Tian was sent out to govern Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the winter ancestral sacrifice at the Imperial Temple, he again asked that reward gifts be cut, starting with the chief ministers and working down. Tang Jie argued that this slighted imperial favor, and Tian was sent out to govern Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 俄提點湖南刑獄，介與司馬光又狀其傾險，改知湖州，徙廬州，治有善跡。

translations.literal: Soon he was made judicial intendant of Hunan. Jie and Sima Guang again memorialized that he was devious and dangerous; his appointment was changed to prefect of Huzhou, then he was transferred to Luzhou, where his governance left good traces.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed judicial intendant of Hunan, but Tang Jie and Sima Guang again reported him as treacherous and dangerous. He was reassigned to Huzhou, then transferred to Luzhou, where his administration left a record of solid achievement.

sentences.zh: 移桂州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 異時蠻使朝貢假道，與方伯抗禮，田獨坐堂上，使引入拜於庭，而犒賄加腆。

translations.literal: In former times, when tribal envoys came to court with tribute and passed through, they treated the regional governor as an equal. Tian alone sat in the hall and had the envoys brought in to bow in the courtyard, yet he added generous gifts and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier days, tribal envoys bearing tribute who passed through treated the regional governor as an equal. Tian alone remained seated in the hall and had the envoys brought in to bow in the courtyard—yet he rewarded them with gifts all the more generously.

sentences.zh: 土豪劉紀、廬豹素為邊患，訖田去，不敢肆。

translations.literal: Local strongmen Liu Ji and Lu Bao had long been border troubles; by the time Tian left, they no longer dared run wild.
translations.idiomatic: The local magnates Liu Ji and Lu Bao had long plagued the frontier, but by the time Tian departed they no longer dared make trouble.

sentences.zh: 京師禁兵來戍，不習風土，往往病於瘴癘，田以兵法訓峒丁而奏罷戍。

translations.literal: Capital garrison troops came to hold the frontier posts; unaccustomed to the local climate, they often fell ill from miasma. Tian trained the cave militia by military methods and memorialized to abolish the garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Capital garrison troops were sent to hold the frontier, but unused to the local climate they often sickened and died of miasmic fever. Tian drilled the cave militia by military methods and memorialized to end the garrison deployment.

sentences.zh: 或告交阯李日尊兵九萬，謀襲特磨道，諸將請益兵，田曰：「交阯兵不滿三萬，必其國有故，張虛聲以嚇我耳。」

translations.literal: Someone reported that Li Rizun of Jiaozhi had ninety thousand troops and planned to strike the Temó route. The generals asked for reinforcements. Tian said, "Jiaozhi's troops number fewer than thirty thousand; there must be trouble in their state—they are raising a false alarm to frighten us."
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Li Rizun of Jiaozhi had ninety thousand men and planned to strike along the Temó route. The generals asked for reinforcements. Tian said, "Jiaozhi cannot field even thirty thousand soldiers. Something must be wrong at home—they are bluffing to scare us."

sentences.zh: 諜既得實，果其兄弟內相殘，懼邊將乘之也。

translations.literal: When spies obtained the facts, it turned out that his brothers were slaughtering one another within the state, and he feared border generals would take advantage of it.
translations.idiomatic: When his scouts confirmed the facts, it proved that rival brothers were tearing the kingdom apart from within, and Li had inflated his numbers for fear our border commanders would exploit the chaos.

sentences.zh: 宜州人魏利安負罪亡命西南龍蕃，從其使入貢，凡十反，至是龍以烈來，復從之。

translations.literal: Wei Li'an of Yizhou, guilty of crime, fled as an outlaw to the Long Fan tribes in the southwest and followed their envoys in tribute missions ten times in all. On this occasion Long Yilie came, and he followed him again.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Li'an of Yizhou, a fugitive guilty of capital crime, had fled to the Long Fan tribes in the southwest and accompanied their tribute missions ten times in all. When Long Yilie came on this occasion, he followed him once again.

sentences.zh: 田因其入謁，詰責之，梟其首，欲並斬以烈，叩頭流血請命。

translations.literal: Tian, taking advantage of his coming to audience, interrogated and rebuked him, displayed his head, and was about to execute Yilie as well. Yilie knocked his head on the ground until it bled, begging for his life.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei came to audience, Tian interrogated and rebuked him, then displayed his severed head. He was about to execute Yilie as well, but Yilie knocked his forehead bloody on the ground, begging for mercy.

sentences.zh: 田曰：「汝罪當死，然事幸在新天子即位赦前，汝自從朝廷乞恩。」

translations.literal: Tian said, "Your crime deserves death, yet fortunately the matter occurred before the new emperor's accession amnesty. You yourself must beg grace from the court."
translations.idiomatic: Tian said, "Your crime deserves death, but fortunately the offense came before the new emperor's accession amnesty. You must plead for mercy from the court yourself."

sentences.zh: 乃密請貸其死。

translations.literal: He then secretly requested that his life be spared.
translations.idiomatic: He then secretly petitioned to spare Yilie's life.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，加直龍圖閣、知廣州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining he was given direct appointment to the Hall of Dragon Designs and appointed prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xining era he was granted direct appointment to the Hall of Dragon Designs and made prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣舊無外郭，民悉野處，田始築東城，環七里，賦功五十萬，兩旬而成。

translations.literal: Guangzhou formerly had no outer wall; the people all lived in the open countryside. Tian first built the eastern wall, encircling seven li, assigned five hundred thousand work units, and completed it in twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou had long lacked an outer wall, and the people lived scattered in the open countryside. Tian built the eastern wall first, a circuit of seven li, mobilizing five hundred thousand work units and finishing in twenty days.

sentences.zh: 初，役人相驚以白虎夜出，田跡知其偽，召戒邏者曰：「今夕有白衣人出入林間者，謹捕之。」

translations.literal: At first the laborers alarmed one another with reports that a white tiger came out at night. Tian traced the matter and knew it was a fraud; he summoned and warned the patrol guards, saying, "Tonight if there is a person in white entering and leaving the woods, arrest him carefully."
translations.idiomatic: At first the laborers panicked one another with rumors of a white tiger abroad at night. Tian investigated and saw through the hoax. He summoned the night patrol and warned them, "If you see a man in white moving through the woods tonight, seize him at once."

sentences.zh: 如言而獲。

translations.literal: It happened as he said, and the man was captured.
translations.idiomatic: It happened just as he said, and the man was caught.

sentences.zh: 城既就，東南微陷，往視之，暴卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: When the wall was finished, the southeast section sank slightly. He went to inspect it and died suddenly, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: When the wall was finished, a section on the southeast sank slightly. He went to inspect it and died suddenly, at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 田為人伉直自喜，好嫚罵，氣陵其下，故死無哀者。

translations.literal: Tian as a man was upright and self-satisfied, fond of contemptuous abuse, and overbearing toward those beneath him; therefore when he died no one mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian was blunt, proud, and fond of hurling contempt at others; he browbeat his subordinates, and so when he died no one grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 然臨政以清，女弟聘馬軍帥王凱，欲售珠犀於廣，顧曰：「南海富諸物，但身為市舶使，不欲自汙爾。」

translations.literal: Yet in governing he was clean. His younger sister was betrothed to the cavalry commander Wang Kai, who wished to sell pearls and rhinoceros horn in Guangzhou. Tian looked at him and said, "The Southern Sea is rich in all goods, but I serve as maritime trade commissioner and do not wish to stain myself."
translations.idiomatic: Yet in office he was incorruptible. His younger sister had married the cavalry commander Wang Kai, who wanted to sell pearls and rhinoceros horn in Guangzhou. Tian told him, "The Southern Sea has every luxury, but I am maritime trade commissioner and have no wish to corrupt myself."

sentences.zh: 作欽賢堂，繪古昔清刺史像，日夕師拜之。

translations.literal: He built the Hall for Revering the Worthy, painted portraits of incorruptible prefects of old, and morning and evening took them as teachers in bowing to them.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Hall for Revering the Worthy, painted portraits of incorruptible prefects of antiquity, and morning and evening bowed to them as his teachers.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾嘗讀其書，以侔古廉吏。

translations.literal: Su Shi once read his writings and ranked him with incorruptible officials of old.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi once read his writings and judged him the equal of the incorruptible officials of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 榮諲，字仲思，濟州任城人。

translations.literal: Rong Yin, style name Zhongsi, was a native of Rencheng in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Yin, courtesy name Zhongsi, was a native of Rencheng in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 父宗範，知信州鉛山縣。

translations.literal: His father Zongfan served as magistrate of Qianshan County in Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zongfan served as magistrate of Qianshan County in Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔罷縣募民采銅，民散為盜，宗範請復如故。

translations.literal: An edict abolished the county's recruitment of people to mine copper; the people scattered and became bandits. Zongfan requested that the former practice be restored.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict abolished the county's system of recruiting commoners to mine copper, the people dispersed and turned to banditry. Zongfan petitioned to restore the former arrangement.

sentences.zh: 真宗嘉異，擢提點江、浙諸路銀銅坑冶，歷官九年。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong praised this as exceptional and promoted him to intendant of silver and copper mines and smelters on the Jiang and Zhe circuits; he held office nine years.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong was greatly impressed and promoted him to intendant of silver and copper mines and smelters on the Jiang and Zhe circuits, where he served nine years.

sentences.zh: 諲舉進士，至鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: Yin passed the jinshi examination and rose to salt and iron judge.
translations.idiomatic: Yin passed the jinshi examination and rose to salt and iron judge.

sentences.zh: 晉州產礬，京城大豪歲輸鐵五萬緡，顓其利，諲請榷於官，自是數入四倍。

translations.literal: Jin Prefecture produced alum; a great magnate of the capital paid fifty thousand strings of iron cash annually and monopolized the profit. Yin requested that the state monopolize it, and from then on revenue quadrupled.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Prefecture produced alum, and a great monopolist of the capital paid fifty thousand strings of cash in iron each year while keeping the profits to himself. Yin petitioned for a state monopoly, and thereafter revenue increased fourfold.

sentences.zh: 為廣東轉運使。

translations.literal: He served as transport commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as transport commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 廣有板步古河路絕險，林箐瘴毒。

translations.literal: In Guangdong the ancient Banbu River route was extremely perilous, with dense forest, bamboo thickets, and miasmic poison.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangdong the ancient Banbu River route was treacherous in the extreme, running through dense forest and bamboo groves thick with miasmic poison.

sentences.zh: 諲開真陽峽，至洸口古徑，作棧道七十間抵清遠，趨廣州，遂為夷塗。

translations.literal: Yin opened Zhenyang Gorge as far as the ancient path at Guangkou, built seventy sections of plank road reaching Qingyuan, and led on to Guangzhou, making it a level highway.
translations.idiomatic: Yin cut through Zhenyang Gorge to the ancient track at Guangkou, built seventy sections of plank road as far as Qingyuan, and opened a smooth route on to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 復入為開封府判官。

translations.literal: He returned to the capital as judge of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as judge of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太康民事浮屠法，相聚祈禳，號「白衣會」，縣捕數十人送府。

translations.literal: The people of Taikang practiced Buddhist rites, gathering to pray for blessings in what was called the White Robe Society; the county arrested several dozen people and sent them to the prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Taikang practiced Buddhist rites, gathering to pray for blessings in a group called the White Robe Society. The county arrested several dozen members and sent them to the prefectural court.

sentences.zh: 尹賈黯疑為妖，請殺其為首者而流其餘，諲持不從，各具議上之。

translations.literal: Prefect Jia An suspected sorcery and requested that the ringleaders be executed and the rest banished. Yin refused to agree and each submitted his own opinion to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Jia An suspected sorcery and asked that the ringleaders be executed and the rest banished. Yin dissented, and each man submitted his own recommendation to the throne.

sentences.zh: 中書是諲議，但流其首而杖餘人。

translations.literal: The Central Secretariat approved Yin's proposal: only the ringleaders were banished and the rest were beaten with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Secretariat sided with Yin: only the ringleaders were banished, and the rest were flogged.

sentences.zh: 加直史館、知澶州。

translations.literal: He was given direct appointment to the Historical Archives and appointed prefect of Chan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted direct appointment to the Historical Archives and made prefect of Chan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 改京東轉運使。

translations.literal: He was changed to transport commissioner of Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed transport commissioner of Jingdong.

sentences.zh: 萊陽產銀砂，民有私采者，事露，安撫使欲論以劫盜。

translations.literal: Laiyang produced silver sand; there were people who mined it privately. When the matter came to light, the pacification commissioner wished to prosecute them as robbers by force.
translations.idiomatic: Laiyang produced silver-bearing sand, and some commoners had been mining it illicitly. When the affair came to light, the pacification commissioner wanted to prosecute them as armed robbers.

sentences.zh: 諲曰：「山澤之利，人得有之，所盜者豈民財耶？」

translations.literal: Yin said, "The profit of mountains and marshes may be had by the people—what they stole was not the people's wealth, was it?"
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "The bounty of hills and marshes is there for anyone to take—what they took was not private property stolen from the people, was it?"

sentences.zh: 貸免甚眾。

translations.literal: Very many were pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: A great many were pardoned as a result.

sentences.zh: 又使成都府路，召為戶部副使，以集賢殿修撰知洪州。

translations.literal: He was again sent on mission to the Chengdu Fu circuit, summoned as Vice Commissioner of the Household Department, and appointed prefect of Hongzhou with the title Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was again dispatched to the Chengdu circuit, then recalled as Vice Commissioner of the Household Department and appointed prefect of Hongzhou with the title Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Talent.

sentences.zh: 以疾故，徙舒州，未至而卒。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was transferred to Shuzhou, but before arriving he died.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced his transfer to Shuzhou, but he died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 累官秘書監，年六十五。

translations.literal: Through accumulated rank he reached Director of the Secretariat, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: By accumulated rank he had risen to Director of the Secretariat; he was sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 李載，字伯熙，黎陽人。

translations.literal: Li Zai, style name Boxi, was a native of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zai, courtesy name Boxi, was a native of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 少苦學，隆暑讀書，置足於水，雖得疾，不舍去。

translations.literal: In youth he studied arduously; in the height of summer while reading he placed his feet in water, and even when he fell ill he would not stop.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied with fierce dedication. Even in midsummer he kept his feet in a basin of water while he read, and when illness came he still would not lay his books aside.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，調冀州推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as judicial assistant in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he was assigned as judicial assistant in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 知大名冠氏縣，府守呂夷簡入相，薦其材，知齊州。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Guanshi County in Daming Prefecture, when the prefect Lu Yijian entered the chief ministership he recommended Zai's talent, and Zai was appointed prefect of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as magistrate of Guanshi County in Daming Prefecture, he was recommended for his ability by the prefect Lu Yijian after Lu entered the chief ministership, and was appointed prefect of Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鈐轄趙瑜使酒毆載，乃扃戶避逸。

translations.literal: The commander Zhao Yu, drunk, beat Zai; Zai then bolted his door to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander Zhao Yu, drunk, assaulted Zai, who bolted his door to escape him.

sentences.zh: 瑜得罪，載坐不舉劾，黜為信陽軍。

translations.literal: When Yu was punished, Zai was implicated for failing to impeach him and was demoted to Xinyang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Yu was punished, Zai was demoted to Xinyang Circuit for failing to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 安撫使錢明逸等為之申理，改常州。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner Qian Mingyi and others pleaded his case for him, and his appointment was changed to Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commissioner Qian Mingyi and others interceded on his behalf, and he was reassigned to Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 知祥符縣，有巫以井泉飲人，云可愈疾，趨者旁午，載杖巫，堙其井。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Xiangfu County, there was a shaman who gave people water from a well to drink, saying it could cure illness; those who rushed to him came in unbroken streams. Zai beat the shaman with the staff and filled in the well.
translations.idiomatic: While magistrate of Xiangfu County, he encountered a shaman who gave people water from a well, claiming it could cure disease; the crowds came in an unbroken stream. Zai had the shaman beaten with the staff and the well filled in.

sentences.zh: 歷知虢州、漣水軍。

translations.literal: He successively governed Guo Prefecture and Lianshui Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of Guo Prefecture and of Lianshui Circuit.

sentences.zh: 載性篤孝，侍母病不解帶，至病亟不能食，載亦不食，母知之，為強食。

translations.literal: Li Zai was deeply filial by nature. While attending his mother's illness he did not undo his belt; when her illness grew critical and she could not eat, Zai also did not eat. When his mother learned of this, she forced him to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zai was profoundly filial. While nursing his ailing mother he never loosened his belt for rest; when she grew so ill she could no longer eat, he refused food as well. Learning of this, she made him eat by force.

sentences.zh: 六為州，一以寬厚稱。

translations.literal: In the six prefectures where he served, he was uniformly known for generosity and lenience.
translations.idiomatic: Across the six prefectures he governed, he was known throughout for his gracious, lenient rule.

sentences.zh: 以光祿卿提舉仙源觀，卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: Serving as Director of the Palace Office for Imperial Sacrifices and supervisor of the Xianyuan Monastery, he died at the age of seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of Director of the Palace Office for Imperial Sacrifices and supervised the Xianyuan Monastery, then died at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 姚渙，字虛州，世家長安。

translations.literal: Yao Huan, style name Xuzhou, came from a distinguished family of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Huan, courtesy name Xuzhou, was from an eminent clan of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，有景徹者，以討平瀘夷，策功為普州刺史，卒，子孫遂家普州。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui, there was one Jing Che, who for suppressing and pacifying the Lu barbarians was rewarded with appointment as prefect of Puzhou; he died, and his descendants then made their home in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang reign of the Sui dynasty, an ancestor named Jing Che, commended for putting down the Lu tribes, was made prefect of Puzhou. After his death his line settled there for good.

sentences.zh: 渙第進士，監益州交子務，發奸隱萬緡，主吏皆當死，渙曰：「戮人以干澤，非吾志也，義不蔽奸而已。」

translations.literal: Huan passed the jinshi examination and supervised the Jiaozi Office in Yizhou. He exposed fraud and concealed funds amounting to ten thousand strings of cash; the chief clerks all deserved death. Huan said: "To kill people in order to seek imperial favor is not my wish; righteousness consists only in not shielding wrongdoing."
translations.idiomatic: After taking his jinshi degree, Huan supervised the Jiaozi Office in Yizhou and uncovered concealed fraud worth ten thousand strings of cash. The senior clerks were all liable for execution. Huan said, "Slaughtering men to curry favor at court is not my intent—I mean only not to cover up crime."

sentences.zh: 請於使者，願不受賞，於是全活者眾。

translations.literal: He petitioned the envoy, asking to forgo reward; thereby many were spared and kept alive.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the imperial envoy to let him refuse any reward, and in this way many lives were spared.

sentences.zh: 知峽州。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宜都民為盜所殘，縣執囚訊服，以獄上。

translations.literal: People of Yidu were slaughtered by bandits; the county seized a prisoner who confessed under interrogation and sent the case up.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits massacred people in Yidu, the county arrested a man who confessed under torture and forwarded the case to higher authority.

sentences.zh: 渙移劾於他有司，居亡何，真盜獲。

translations.literal: Huan transferred the impeachment to another agency; before long, the real bandits were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Huan referred the indictment to another office; not long afterward the real culprits were caught.

sentences.zh: 大江漲溢，渙前戒民徙儲積、遷高阜，及城沒，無溺者。

translations.literal: The great river swelled and overflowed; Huan had beforehand warned the people to move their stored grain and relocate to higher ground, and when the city was submerged, none drowned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yangzi rose in flood, Huan had already warned the people to move their stores to high ground. When the city went under, no one drowned.

sentences.zh: 因相地形築子城、埽臺，為木岸七十丈，繚以長堤，楗以薪石，厥後江漲不為害，民德之。

translations.literal: Accordingly he surveyed the terrain and built an inner city wall and a revetment platform, constructing a wooden embankment seventy zhang long, girded with a long dike and secured with brushwood and stone; thereafter river floods did no harm, and the people were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: He then studied the lie of the land and built an inner wall and flood-control platform—a seventy-zhang timber revetment ringed by a long levee, shored up with brush and stone. After that the river's rise no longer brought disaster, and the people blessed his name.

sentences.zh: 徙知涪州，賓化夷多犯境，渙施恩信拊納，酋豪爭羅拜廷下，訖渙去無警。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Fu Prefecture. The Binhua Yi frequently raided the border; Huan applied benevolence and trust to win them over, and chieftains competed to bow in prostration before his hall; until Huan departed there were no alarms.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Fu Prefecture, he found the Binhua Yi frequently crossing the border. Huan treated them with kindness and good faith, and tribal chiefs thronged his hall to prostrate themselves in submission. For the rest of his tenure the frontier stayed quiet.

sentences.zh: 終光祿卿，年六十七。

translations.literal: He ended his career as Director of the Palace Office for Imperial Sacrifices, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as Director of the Palace Office for Imperial Sacrifices at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 朱景，字伯晦，河南偃師人。

translations.literal: Zhu Jing, style name Bohui, was a native of Yanshi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jing, courtesy name Bohui, came from Yanshi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，調滎澤簿。

translations.literal: Having passed the jinshi examination, he was assigned as registrar of Rongze.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he was posted as registrar of Rongze.

sentences.zh: 西方用兵，詔侍從館閣舉縣令，景預選，知隴州汧源縣。

translations.literal: When war was waged in the west, an edict ordered attendants and institute scholars to recommend county magistrates; Jing was preselected and appointed magistrate of Qianyuan County in Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the western campaigns, the throne ordered court attendants and Hanlin scholars to nominate county magistrates; Jing was chosen and appointed magistrate of Qianyuan in Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷知汝州。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to serve as prefect of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several postings to become prefect of Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 葉驛道遠，隸囚為送者所虐，多死，俗傳為「葉家關」，景重禁以絕其患。

translations.literal: The Ye relay station was far away; convicts assigned as escorts were abused by the couriers and many died—a custom spoken of as "Ye Family Pass." Jing strictly prohibited this and ended the abuse.
translations.idiomatic: The Ye relay route was long and arduous; prisoners drafted as escorts were mistreated by the runners, and many died—people called it the "Ye Family Pass." Jing enforced stern prohibitions and ended the scourge.

sentences.zh: 擢知壽州，秩祿視提點刑獄。

translations.literal: He was promoted to serve as prefect of Shou Prefecture, with rank and stipend equal to a regional inspector of penal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to prefect of Shouzhou, he held rank and salary equivalent to a circuit judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 始至，亟發廩振給，以勸富者出積穀，所活數萬。

translations.literal: As soon as he arrived, he immediately opened the granaries for relief distribution to encourage the wealthy to release stored grain; tens of thousands were saved.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he immediately opened the public granaries and distributed relief, urging the wealthy to release hoarded grain as well; tens of thousands of lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 城西居民三千室，建請築外郭環入之，公私稱便。

translations.literal: Three thousand households of residents west of the city petitioned to build an outer wall enclosing them within it; both public and private interests praised the convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand households west of the city asked that a new outer wall be built to take them in; officials and commoners alike praised the convenience.

sentences.zh: 再遷光祿卿。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Director of the Palace Office for Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Director of the Palace Office for Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，病革，自占遺表，呼其子光庭操筆書之。

translations.literal: In the early Xining era, gravely ill, he himself composed his final memorial and called his son Guangting to take up the brush and write it down.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xining era, as his illness turned fatal, he dictated his final memorial and had his son Guangting write it out.

sentences.zh: 其略云：「切聞河北水災、地震，陛下當減膳避殿，齋居加省，召二府大臣朝夕諮訪闕失，思所以弭咎。」

translations.literal: Its gist read: "I have heard with deep concern of floods and earthquakes in Hebei. Your Majesty ought to reduce your meals, withdraw from the main halls, dwell in fasting and added self-restraint, summon the two councils' senior ministers morning and evening to consult on failures and omissions, and consider means to avert the calamity."
translations.idiomatic: In substance it said: "I have learned with alarm of flooding and earthquakes in Hebei. Your Majesty should take simpler meals and retire from the main palace halls, live in abstinent seclusion, and summon the chief ministers of both councils daily to discuss what has gone wrong and how to turn aside Heaven's displeasure."

sentences.zh: 凡數百言，無一語求恩。

translations.literal: It ran to several hundred words, not one phrase seeking favor.
translations.idiomatic: The whole ran to several hundred words, and not a single line asked any favor for himself or his family.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 詔加賻贈，錄其子以官。

translations.literal: An edict added funeral gifts and bestowed offices upon his son.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered additional funeral gifts and granted his son an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 子 光庭

translations.literal: Son: Guangting.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Guangting.

sentences.zh: 光庭，字公掞，十歲能屬文。

translations.literal: Guangting, style name Gongshan, could compose prose at the age of ten.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting, courtesy name Gongshan, was composing essays by the age of ten.

sentences.zh: 辭父蔭擢第，調萬年主簿。

translations.literal: Declining his father's privilege, he passed the examination on his own merit and was assigned as chief clerk of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: Refusing the privilege of his father's rank, he passed the examinations on his own and was appointed chief clerk of Wannian County.

sentences.zh: 數攝邑，人以「明鏡」稱。

translations.literal: He several times acted as magistrate of counties; people called him the "Bright Mirror."
translations.idiomatic: Having served repeatedly as acting county magistrate, people nicknamed him the "Bright Mirror."

sentences.zh: 歷四縣令。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of four counties in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He held magistracies in four counties in turn.

sentences.zh: 曾孝寬以才薦，神宗召見，問欲再舉安南之師。

translations.literal: Zeng Xiaokuan recommended him for talent; Emperor Shenzong summoned him for an audience and asked whether he wished to raise troops against Annam again.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for his ability by Zeng Xiaokuan, Guangting was summoned before Emperor Shenzong, who asked whether he favored another campaign against Annam.

sentences.zh: 光庭對曰：「願陛下勿以人類畜之。

translations.literal: Guangting replied: "I wish Your Majesty would not keep them as mere livestock among men.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting answered, "I would ask Your Majesty not to treat human beings as beasts of burden.

sentences.zh: 蓋得其地不可居，得其民不可使，何益於廣土辟地也。」

translations.literal: For though one may gain their land it cannot be inhabited, and though one may gain their people they cannot be employed—what benefit is there in broadening territory and opening new lands?"
translations.idiomatic: Even if you take their land, you cannot live there; even if you take their people, you cannot govern them. What good is conquest when the land cannot be settled and the people cannot be ruled?"

sentences.zh: 又問治何經，對曰：「少從孫復學《春秋》。」

translations.literal: The Emperor again asked which classic he studied for governance; he replied: "In youth I studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under Sun Fu."
translations.idiomatic: Asked which classic guided his statecraft, he replied, "In my youth I studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under Sun Fu."

sentences.zh: 又問：「今中外有所聞乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor again asked: "Have you heard anything from within or without the court?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked further, "Have you heard anything of concern inside or outside the court?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下更張法度，臣下奉行或非聖意，故有便有不便。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty has reshaped laws and institutions; subordinates in carrying them out sometimes miss the sage intent, hence there are conveniences and inconveniences.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your Majesty has changed the laws and institutions. When officials carry them out imperfectly, some measures work and others do not.

sentences.zh: 誠能去其不便，則天下受福矣。」

translations.literal: If those that are inconvenient can truly be removed, then all under Heaven will receive blessing."
translations.idiomatic: Remove what does not work, and the realm will be the better for it."

sentences.zh: 帝以其言為疏闊，不用。

translations.literal: The Emperor regarded his words as loose and broad-minded and did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor judged his counsel too vague and did not appoint him to office.

sentences.zh: 簽書河陽判官，從呂大防於長安幕府。

translations.literal: He served as signing aide to the magistrate of Heyang and followed Lü Dafang in the Chang'an headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: As signing aide to the prefect of Heyang, he served on Lü Dafang's staff in the Chang'an headquarters.

sentences.zh: 五路出師討西夏，雍為都會，事倚以辦，調發期會甚急，光庭每執不從。

translations.literal: When the five routes marched out to campaign against Western Xia, Yong was the grand depot and affairs relied on him for completion; mobilization deadlines were extremely urgent, but Guangting repeatedly held firm and refused compliance.
translations.idiomatic: During the five-route campaign against Western Xia, Yongzhou served as the main supply hub and everything depended on its speed of delivery. Deadlines were brutal, but Guangting repeatedly refused to go along.

sentences.zh: 使者怒，將加以乏興罪，光庭求免去，大防為之解。

translations.literal: The envoy grew angry and was about to charge him with the crime of failing to supply the army; Guangting asked to be relieved, and Dafang interceded on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial envoy threatened to charge him with dereliction of supply duty; Guangting asked to be dismissed, and Dafang pleaded his case.

sentences.zh: 河北饑，遣持節行視，即發廩振民；

translations.literal: When Hebei suffered famine, he was dispatched with imperial credentials to inspect on circuit; he immediately opened the granaries to relieve the people.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck Hebei, he was sent with imperial credentials on an inspection tour and at once opened the granaries to feed the people.

sentences.zh: 而議者以耗先帝積年兵食之蓄，改左司員外郎。

translations.literal: Critics held that this depleted the stores of military provisions accumulated over years under the former emperor, and he was transferred to Left Secretary Outer Section Member.
translations.idiomatic: Critics complained that he had drawn down stores of grain amassed for the military under the previous emperor, and he was reassigned as Outer Section Member of the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷太常少卿，拜侍御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 論蔡確怨謗之罪，確貶新州。

translations.literal: He impeached Cai Que for the crime of resentment and slander; Que was demoted to Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He prosecuted Cai Que for slander and malice, and Que was banished to Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 拜右諫議大夫、給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Remonstrance Grand Master and Chief Reviser of Drafts.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Remonstrance Grand Master and Chief Reviser of Drafts.

sentences.zh: 乞補外，除集賢殿修撰、知亳州。

translations.literal: He requested appointment outside the capital and was made Compiler at the Hall of Worthies and prefect of Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a provincial post and was appointed Compiler in the Hall of Worthies and prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 數月召還，復為給事中。

translations.literal: After several months he was recalled and again served as Chief Reviser of Drafts.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was recalled and restored as Chief Reviser of Drafts.

sentences.zh: 坐封還劉摯免相制，復落職守亳。

translations.literal: For returning the draft edict dismissing Liu Zhi from the chancellorship sealed back unapproved, he was again stripped of office and retained only prefect of Bo.
translations.idiomatic: For returning Liu Zhi's dismissal edict unapproved, he lost his central post and was left to govern Bozhou alone.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，徙潞州，加集賢院學士。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Lu Prefecture, with the added title of Hanlin Academician of the Hall of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was transferred to Luzhou and given the additional title of Hanlin Academician of the Hall of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 鄰境旱饑，流民入境者踵接，光庭日為食以食之，常至暮，自不暇食，遂感疾，猶自力視事。

translations.literal: Drought and famine afflicted neighboring circuits; refugees entering the border followed one after another. Guangting daily prepared food to feed them, often until evening, with no time to eat himself; he thus fell ill, yet still forced himself to attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring circuits suffered drought and famine, and refugees poured across the border. Every day Guangting had food prepared for them, often working until dusk without eating himself. He fell ill but continued to carry on his duties.

sentences.zh: 出禱雨，拜不能興，再宿而卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: Going out to pray for rain, he could not rise after bowing; two nights later he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to pray for rain, collapsed while bowing, and died two days later at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，追貶柳州別駕。

translations.literal: In the Shaosheng era he was posthumously demoted to assistant prefect of Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng reign he was posthumously demoted to assistant prefect of Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 元符初，又停錮其諸子。

translations.literal: In the early Yuanfu era, his sons were again placed under prohibition and confinement.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanfu reign his sons were barred from office as well.

sentences.zh: 光庭始學於胡瑗，瑗告以為學之本在於忠信，故終身行之。

translations.literal: Guangting had first studied under Hu Yuan; Yuan told him that the root of learning lay in loyalty and trustworthiness, and so he practiced these throughout his life.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting had begun his studies with Hu Yuan, who taught that loyalty and good faith were the foundation of learning; he lived by that teaching all his life.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，復其官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong took the throne, his offices were restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong succeeded to the throne, Guangting's official titles were restored.

sentences.zh: 李琮，字獻甫，江寧人。

translations.literal: Li Cong, style name Xianfu, was a native of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cong, courtesy name Xianfu, came from Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，調寧國軍推官。

translations.literal: He attained the jinshi degree and was assigned as judicial assistant in the Ningguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he was posted as judicial assistant in Ningguo prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州庾積穀腐敗，轉運使移州散於民，俾至秋償新者。

translations.literal: Grain stored in the prefecture's granaries had rotted; the transport commissioner ordered the prefecture to distribute it to the people, requiring repayment with new grain by autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Grain in the prefecture granaries had spoiled, and the transport commissioner ordered it distributed to the people on the understanding they would repay with fresh grain in autumn.

sentences.zh: 守將行之，琮曰：「穀不可食，強與民責而償之，將何以堪。」

translations.literal: The prefectural commander was about to carry this out; Cong said: "The grain is inedible—if we force it on the people and then demand repayment, how can they bear it?"
translations.idiomatic: The prefect was ready to comply when Cong objected: "This grain is unfit to eat. If you force it on the people and still demand repayment, how can they endure it?"

sentences.zh: 持不下，守愧謝而止。

translations.literal: He held firm and would not issue it; the prefect, ashamed, apologized and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: He blocked the order from being issued; the prefect, ashamed, apologized and dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 呂公著尹開封，薦知陽武縣。

translations.literal: When Lü Gongzhu governed Kaifeng, he recommended Cong for appointment as magistrate of Yangwu County.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as prefect of Kaifeng, Lü Gongzhu recommended him as magistrate of Yangwu County.

sentences.zh: 役法初行，琮處畫盡理，旁近民相率撾登聞鼓，願視以為則。

translations.literal: When the corvée labor law was first put into effect, Cong's arrangements were entirely reasonable; people in neighboring districts successively beat the Denunciation Drum at the palace gate, asking to use his district as their model.
translations.idiomatic: When the labor-service law first took effect, Cong's implementation was so fair that people from neighboring districts thronged the palace gate beating the Denunciation Drum, asking that their counties follow Yangwu's example.

sentences.zh: 徽宗召對，擢利州路、江東轉運判官。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong summoned him for audience and promoted him to transport commissioner-assessor for Lizhou Circuit and Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience by Huizong, he was promoted to transport commissioner-assessor for Lizhou and Jiangdong circuits.

sentences.zh: 行部至宣城，按民田詭稱逃絕者九千戶，他縣皆然。

translations.literal: On inspection tour he reached Xuancheng and investigated farmland falsely reported as abandoned—nine thousand households; other counties were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Touring his jurisdiction he found nine thousand households in Xuancheng alone whose land had been falsely declared abandoned, and the same pattern repeated in county after county.

sentences.zh: 言於朝，命以戶部判官使江、浙，選強明吏立賞剔抉。

translations.literal: He reported to court; he was ordered as Ministry of Revenue commissioner-assessor to Jiang and Zhe, selecting capable officials and establishing rewards for uncovering hidden land.
translations.idiomatic: He reported this to court and was dispatched as a Ministry of Revenue commissioner to Jiangsu and Zhejiang with orders to appoint sharp officials and offer rewards for exposing concealed land.

sentences.zh: 吏幸賞，以多為功，琮亦因是希進，民患苦之，得緡錢百餘萬。

translations.literal: Officials, hoping for rewards, took large numbers as merit; Cong also sought advancement thereby; the people suffered greatly, and over a million strings of cash were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy officials inflated their numbers to win rewards, and Cong used the drive to advance his career. The people were crushed by it, yet more than a million strings of cash were extracted.

sentences.zh: 進度支判官，頒職式於諸道。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Revenue Section commissioner-assessor and issued standard procedures to all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to commissioner-assessor in the Revenue Section, he issued uniform regulations to every circuit.

sentences.zh: 淮南賦入甲它部，以為轉運副使，徙梓州路。

translations.literal: Huainan's tax receipts ranked first among departments; he was made vice transport commissioner and transferred to Zizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Because Huainan's tax revenue led all regions, he was made vice transport commissioner, then transferred to Zizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，言者論其括隱稅之害，黜知吉州。

translations.literal: In the early Yuanyou era, critics impeached the harm of his land-registration and concealed-tax policies, and he was demoted to prefect of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou reign critics denounced his hidden-land tax campaign, and he was demoted to prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 御史呂陶又言巴蜀科折已重，琮復強民輸稅，且無得以奇數併合，人尤咨怨。

translations.literal: Censor Lü Tao further stated that levies and conversion in Ba-Shu were already heavy; Cong again forced the people to pay taxes, and moreover did not allow odd fractions to be combined—people were especially resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Lü Tao added that Sichuan's tax quotas and grain conversion were already crushing, yet Cong again forced payment and refused to let people combine odd sums—all of which stirred deep resentment.

sentences.zh: 於是凡以括田受賞者悉奪之。

translations.literal: Thereupon all who had received rewards for registering hidden fields had those rewards revoked.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, everyone rewarded for the land-registration drive had their honors stripped.

sentences.zh: 歷相、洪、潞三州。

translations.literal: He served in succession as prefect of Xiang, Hong, and Lu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He governed three prefectures in turn: Xiang, Hong, and Lu.

sentences.zh: 潞有謀亂者，為書期日揭道上，部使者聞之懼，檄索奸甚亟。

translations.literal: In Lu there were plotters who posted a letter on the road setting a date; the circuit envoy heard of it in fear and issued urgent orders to hunt down conspirators.
translations.idiomatic: At Luzhou conspirators posted a letter on the road setting a date for revolt. The circuit intendant panicked and issued urgent orders to hunt them down.

sentences.zh: 琮置不問，以是日置酒高會，訖無他。

translations.literal: Cong paid no heed; on that very day he held a grand banquet with wine, and in the end nothing else occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Cong ignored the alarm, held a grand feast on the very day named in the letter, and nothing happened.

sentences.zh: 入為太府卿，遷戶部侍郎，以寶文閣待制知杭州、永興軍、河南、瀛州。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Grand Director of the Office of Imperial Manufactories, was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, and served as Pavilion Drafting Gentleman-at-Large governing Hangzhou, Yongxing Army, Henan, and Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Called to the capital, he became Grand Director of the Office of Imperial Manufactories and Vice Minister of Revenue, then served as Pavilion Drafting Gentleman-at-Large in Hangzhou, Yongxing, Henan, and Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 琮長於吏治，而所至主於掊克，為士論嗤鄙。

translations.literal: Cong was skilled in administrative governance, but wherever he went he chiefly practiced extortion, and was scorned in literati opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Though adept at administration, Cong was known everywhere for squeezing the people, and men of learning held him in contempt.

sentences.zh: 子回，紹興初參知政事。

translations.literal: His son Hui served as vice grand councilor in the early Shaoxing era.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui became vice grand councilor early in the Shaoxing reign.

sentences.zh: 朱壽隆

translations.literal: Zhu Shoulong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shoulong.

sentences.zh: 朱壽隆，字仲山，密州諸城人。

translations.literal: Zhu Shoulong, style name Zhongshan, was a native of Zhucheng in Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shoulong, courtesy name Zhongshan, came from Zhucheng in Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 以蔭知九隴縣。

translations.literal: Through inherited privilege he became magistrate of Jiulong County.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office by hereditary privilege as magistrate of Jiulong County.

sentences.zh: 吏告民一家七人以火死，壽隆曰：「寧有盡室就焚無一脫者，殆必有奸。」

translations.literal: A clerk reported that seven people of one family had died by fire; Shoulong said: "How can an entire household burn to death with not one escape—there must surely be foul play."
translations.idiomatic: When a clerk reported that seven members of one family had died in a fire, Shoulong said, "No whole household burns to ash without a single survivor—someone must be hiding murder behind the flames."

sentences.zh: 逾月獲盜，果殺其人而縱火也。

translations.literal: More than a month later the bandit was captured; it turned out he had killed the people and then set the fire.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the culprit was caught: he had murdered the family and set the fire to cover it up.

sentences.zh: 知宿州，宿多劇盜，至白晝被甲剽攻，郡縣不能制。

translations.literal: As prefect of Su Prefecture, he found Su had many fierce bandits who even by day wore armor for plundering raids; prefectures and counties could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Suzhou he found the region overrun by ruthless bandits who raided in broad daylight in armor, beyond the reach of local officials.

sentences.zh: 壽隆設方略耳目，捕斬千餘人。

translations.literal: Shoulong set up stratagems and informants and captured and executed more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shoulong built a network of agents and traps, capturing and executing more than a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 擢提點廣西刑獄。

translations.literal: He was promoted to regional inspector of penal affairs for Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to circuit judicial commissioner for Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 嶺外新經儂寇，修營城障，貴州虐用其人，不能聊生。

translations.literal: The Lingnan region had newly suffered the Nong rebellions; fortifications and garrison walls were under repair, and Guizhou abused its laborers until they could barely survive.
translations.idiomatic: The far south had just been ravaged by the Nong rebellions. While rebuilding walls and fortifications, Guizhou worked its people so brutally they could barely live.

sentences.zh: 壽隆馳詣州，械守送獄，奏黜之。

translations.literal: Shoulong galloped to the prefecture, fettered the prefect and sent him to prison, and memorialized for his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Shoulong raced to Guizhou, had the prefect arrested, and memorialized for his removal.

sentences.zh: 老稚婦女遭亂，流轉不能自還者，檄所在資送其還。

translations.literal: For the old, the young, and women who had suffered the turmoil and wandered unable to return home, he issued orders to local authorities to supply funds and escort them back.
translations.idiomatic: For elders, children, and women displaced by the fighting who could not find their way home, he ordered local officials to provide funds and send them back.

sentences.zh: 舊制，溪蠻侵暴羈縻州，雖殺人無得仇報，壽隆請聽相償，蠻始畏戢。

translations.literal: Under the old system, when Stream barbarians raided attached prefectures, even if they killed people no vengeance could be taken; Shoulong requested that mutual compensation be allowed, and only then did the barbarians begin to fear and restrain themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Under old rules, when tribal peoples from the streams attacked the frontier prefectures, even murder went unpunished. Shoulong obtained permission for blood compensation, and only then did the tribes begin to fear restraint.

sentences.zh: 歷鹽鐵度支判官、夔路轉運使。

translations.literal: He served successively as salt and iron revenue commissioner-assessor and transport commissioner for Kuizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as commissioner-assessor in the Salt and Iron and Revenue Sections and as transport commissioner of Kuizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 巴峽地隘，民困於役，免其不應法者千五百人。

translations.literal: Ba Gorge lands were narrow and constricted; the people were exhausted by corvée labor; he exempted fifteen hundred who did not meet legal requirements.
translations.idiomatic: The Ba Gorge country was cramped and its people crushed by labor levies; he exempted fifteen hundred men who had been drafted in violation of the law.

sentences.zh: 復為鹽鐵判官、京東轉運使，賜三品服。

translations.literal: He again served as salt and iron commissioner-assessor and transport commissioner of Jingdong Circuit, and was granted third-rank court dress.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to service as salt and iron commissioner-assessor and transport commissioner of Jingdong, receiving third-rank court robes.

sentences.zh: 歲惡民移，壽隆諭大姓富室畜為田僕，舉貸立息，官為置籍索之，貧富交利。

translations.literal: In a bad harvest year people migrated; Shoulong urged great clans and wealthy households to employ them as farm servants, extend loans at established interest, and have the government keep registers to collect repayment—rich and poor alike benefited.
translations.idiomatic: During a failed harvest year, as people drifted away in search of work, Shoulong urged wealthy landowners to take them on as farm hands, lend at fixed interest, and keep official registers of the loans so debts could be recovered—benefiting both rich and poor.

sentences.zh: 以少府監知揚州，卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: Serving as Director of the Office of Imperial Manufactories while governing Yang Prefecture, he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of the Office of Imperial Manufactories while governing Yangzhou, and died at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 壽隆為人和厚，接談怡怡，必當於理，而不屈於權貴。

translations.literal: Shoulong was mild and generous in person; in conversation he was serene and agreeable, always hitting what was reasonable, yet never bowing before the powerful and noble.
translations.idiomatic: Shoulong was warm and generous by nature. In conversation he was gentle and courteous, always spoke to the point, and never yielded to power or wealth.

sentences.zh: 狄青討賊，欲殺裨將不用命者數人，壽隆極論罪不當死。

translations.literal: When Di Qing was suppressing bandits, he wished to execute several subordinate generals who had disobeyed orders; Shoulong argued forcefully that their crimes did not merit death.
translations.idiomatic: While Di Qing was campaigning against the rebels, he intended to put several insubordinate subordinate generals to death. Shoulong argued strenuously that their offenses did not warrant capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 孫沔在坐，曰：「儂賊害民萬計，此何足惜。」

translations.literal: Sun Mian, who was present, said: "The Nong bandits harmed tens of thousands of people—what is there to regret in this?"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mian, who was present, said, "The Nong rebels slaughtered tens of thousands of our people—why should we spare these men?"

sentences.zh: 壽隆曰：「王師之來以除民害，顧可效賊為暴邪？」

translations.literal: Shoulong said: "The imperial army came to remove harm from the people—how could we imitate the bandits in committing violence?"
translations.idiomatic: Shoulong replied, "The imperial army came to deliver the people from harm—are we to imitate the rebels and become tyrants ourselves?"

sentences.zh: 青感其言而止。

translations.literal: Qing was moved by his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his words, Qing abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 盧士宏

translations.literal: Lu Shihong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shihong.

sentences.zh: 盧士宏，字子高，新鄭人。

translations.literal: Lu Shihong, style name Zigao, was a native of Xinzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shihong, courtesy name Zigao, came from Xinzheng.

sentences.zh: 以父任屢更州縣，所至著清名。

translations.literal: Through his father's office he was repeatedly transferred among prefectures and counties; wherever he went he earned a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Entering service through his father's privilege, he served in one prefecture and county after another, earning a reputation for clean government wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 知信陽軍。

translations.literal: He governed Xinyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as military prefect of Xinyang.

sentences.zh: 官捕為妖術者，餘黨懼及，群聚山谷間，士宏請減其罪招之，即相率歸命。

translations.literal: Officials were arresting those who practiced sorcery; the remaining accomplices feared being implicated and gathered together in mountain valleys. Shihong requested that their sentences be reduced to summon them, and they came forward in succession to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When officials began arresting practitioners of sorcery, the remaining followers feared they would be swept up and fled into the hills. Shihong petitioned to reduce their penalties as an inducement to surrender, and they came forward one after another to submit.

sentences.zh: 徙知漢州，校實民產，使力役不濫，人德之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Han Prefecture; he verified the people's property holdings so that corvée labor was not over-assigned, and the people were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Han Prefecture, he audited household property so that labor levies were not excessive, and the people were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 又知洋州。

translations.literal: He also governed Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先是，圭田多虛籍。

translations.literal: Before this, many top-grade private fields were on false registers.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, many top-grade private landholdings had been falsely registered.

sentences.zh: 士宏考校，令隨實以輸，自部使者而下，皆十損七八。

translations.literal: Shihong examined and verified the records, requiring payment according to actual holdings; from the circuit envoy down, all lost seven or eight tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Shihong audited the registers and required payments to match actual holdings. From the circuit commissioner on down, everyone lost seven or eight tenths of what they had claimed.

sentences.zh: 文彥博、包拯以廉能薦，由三司開拆司擢夔州路轉運使，遂知廣州。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo and Bao Zheng recommended him for integrity and ability; from the open-and-check office of the Three Sections he was promoted to transport commissioner of Kuizhou Circuit, and then governed Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Wen Yanbo and Bao Zheng for integrity and competence, he rose from the open-and-check office of the Three Sections to transport commissioner of Kuizhou Circuit and then became prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 或傳安南舟數百泊海中，將為寇，嶺徼驚搖。

translations.literal: Some reported that several hundred Anam ships were anchored offshore and were about to become raiders; the Ling border was shaken with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread that several hundred Annamese ships lay at anchor offshore, poised to raid the coast, and the Lingnan frontier was thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 士宏灼其非，是日，從賓客宴遊為樂，民賴以安。

translations.literal: Shihong clearly saw this was untrue; that very day he went with guests to feast and roam for pleasure, and the people relied on this and were reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Shihong saw at once that the report was false. That very day he went out feasting and sightseeing with his guests, and the people took heart from his calm and felt secure again.

sentences.zh: 受代還，引疾丐便郡，知鄭州。

translations.literal: When relieved of office he returned, citing illness to request a convenient prefecture, and governed Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After completing his term he returned home, then cited illness to request a less demanding post and was appointed prefect of Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以光祿卿致仕。

translations.literal: Before long, he retired as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he retired with the rank of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 凡衣衾棺槨之制，皆有遺命，戒諸子勿為銘誌。

translations.literal: For all matters of clothing, bedding, coffin, and inner casket, he left instructions, admonishing his sons not to compose epitaphs or inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: He left detailed instructions for his burial garments, bedding, coffin, and inner casket, and forbade his sons to commission an epitaph or memorial inscription.

sentences.zh: 單煦，字孟陽，平原人。

translations.literal: Dan Xu, style name Mengyang, was a native of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dan Xu, courtesy name Mengyang, came from Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，知洛陽縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and became magistrate of Luoyang County.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he served as magistrate of Luoyang County.

sentences.zh: 民以妖幻傳相教授，煦跡捕戮三十餘人，當得上賞，不肯言。

translations.literal: The people were teaching one another sorcery and illusions; Xu tracked them down and executed more than thirty, for which he deserved a high reward, but he refused to report it.
translations.idiomatic: When the people began teaching one another sorcery and trickery, Xu tracked down and executed more than thirty offenders—an achievement that merited a high commendation, but he never mentioned it.

sentences.zh: 轉知昌州，時詔城蜀治，煦以蜀地負山帶江，一旦毀籬垣而興板築，其費巨萬，非民力所堪，請但築子城。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Chang Prefecture; at the time an edict ordered fortifying the Shu dominions. Xu argued that Shu territory was backed by mountains and ringed by rivers—to suddenly tear down fence walls and build ramparts would cost tens of thousands, beyond what the people's strength could bear—and requested only that a secondary fort be built.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Chang Prefecture during an edict to fortify the Shu region, Xu argued that with its mountains behind and rivers before it, tearing down existing walls to build new ramparts would cost a fortune the people could not sustain. He asked instead to build only an inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 轉運使即移諸郡如其議。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner immediately forwarded orders to all prefectures in accordance with his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner immediately circulated orders to every prefecture adopting his plan.

sentences.zh: 徙清平軍使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as military commissioner of Qingping.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as military commissioner of Qingping.

sentences.zh: 有二盜殺人，捕治不承，煦縱使之食，甲食之既，乙不下咽，執而訊之，果殺人者。

translations.literal: Two thieves had killed someone; captured and interrogated, they would not confess. Xu released them to eat; A finished eating, while B could not swallow. Seized and questioned, B proved to be the killer.
translations.idiomatic: Two thieves had committed murder but would not confess under interrogation. Xu let them eat together: the first finished his meal, but the second could not swallow a bite. Xu seized the second and questioned him, and he proved to be the killer.

sentences.zh: 為御史臺推直官，江南人誣轉運使呂昌齡以賄，中丞張訊而論之。

translations.literal: As investigating officer of the Censorate, he handled a case in which a man from Jiangnan falsely accused transport commissioner Lü Changling of bribery; Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhang tried and prosecuted the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as investigating officer of the Censorate, he took up a case in which a man from Jiangnan had falsely accused transport commissioner Lü Changling of bribery. Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhang had already begun the prosecution.

sentences.zh: 鞫未就，敕煦往治，煦不肯阿其長，卒直昌齡。

translations.literal: Before the trial was finished, an edict ordered Xu to take over the case; he refused to curry favor with his superior and ultimately vindicated Changling.
translations.idiomatic: Before the trial was complete, an edict assigned the case to Xu. He refused to defer to his superior and ultimately cleared Changling of all charges.

sentences.zh: 乞外遷，知濮、合二州。

translations.literal: He requested an outward transfer and governed Pu and He Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a provincial appointment and served as prefect of Pu and He Prefectures in succession.

sentences.zh: 合居涪、漢間，夏秋患於淫潦，煦築東堤以禦之。

translations.literal: He Prefecture lay between the Fu and Han Rivers; in summer and autumn it suffered from excessive flooding; Xu built an eastern dike to defend against it.
translations.idiomatic: He Prefecture lay between the Fu and Han Rivers and suffered chronic summer and autumn flooding. Xu built an eastern dike to hold the waters back.

sentences.zh: 赤水縣鹽井涸，奏蠲其賦。

translations.literal: The salt well in Chishui County dried up; he memorialized to remit its tax.
translations.idiomatic: When the salt well in Chishui County ran dry, he memorialized for a remission of its tax levy.

sentences.zh: 累官光祿卿，卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: He rose to the rank of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually reached the rank of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and died at seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 煦友愛兄熙，兄嘗毆人至死，未有知者。

translations.literal: Xu was devoted to his elder brother Xi; the elder brother had once beaten a man to death, and no one knew.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was deeply devoted to his elder brother Xi, who had once beaten a man to death without anyone discovering it.

sentences.zh: 煦曰：「家貧親老，仰兄以養，義當代之死。」

translations.literal: Xu said: "Our family is poor and our parents are old; we depend on my elder brother to support them—in duty I should die in his place."
translations.idiomatic: Xu said, "Our family is poor and our parents are old. We depend on my brother to support them—it is my duty to die in his place."

sentences.zh: 即趨詣鬥所以待捕。

translations.literal: He immediately rushed to the place of the fight to await arrest.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately went to the scene of the fight and waited to be taken into custody.

sentences.zh: 已而死者蘇，驚問之，煦以情告。

translations.literal: Presently the dead man revived; startled, he asked what had happened, and Xu told him the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the victim revived. Astonished, he asked what had happened, and Xu told him the whole story.

sentences.zh: 其人感歎，遂輟訟。

translations.literal: The man was moved and withdrew the lawsuit.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved, the man dropped his suit.

sentences.zh: 楊仲元

translations.literal: Yang Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 楊仲元，字舜明，管城人。

translations.literal: Yang Zhongyuan, style name Shunming, was a native of Guancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhongyuan, courtesy name Shunming, came from Guancheng.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調宛丘主簿。

translations.literal: He attained the jinshi degree and was appointed chief clerk of Wanqiu.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he was appointed chief clerk of Wanqiu.

sentences.zh: 民訴旱，守拒之，曰：「邑未嘗旱，狡吏導民而然。」

translations.literal: The people petitioned about drought; the prefect refused, saying: "The district has never suffered drought—a crafty clerk led the people to this."
translations.idiomatic: When the people petitioned about drought, the prefect refused them, saying, "This district has never known drought—a scheming clerk put the people up to this."

sentences.zh: 仲元白之曰：「野無青草，公日宴黃堂，宜不能知，但一出郊可見矣。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan reported to him: "There is no green grass in the fields; the lord daily feasts in the yellow hall—you truly could not know—but step outside the city and it can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan reported to him, "There is no green grass in the fields. You feast daily in the hall of office and could hardly know—but walk outside the walls and you will see it for yourself.

sentences.zh: 狡吏非他，實仲元也。」

translations.literal: The crafty clerk is none other than myself."
translations.idiomatic: The scheming clerk is none other than myself."

sentences.zh: 竟免其稅。

translations.literal: In the end the tax was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the tax was remitted.

sentences.zh: 知澤州沁水縣，民持物來輸者，視其價稍增之，餘則下其估。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Qinshui County in Ze Prefecture, when people brought goods for delivery he slightly raised the valuation for those items, and lowered estimates for the rest.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Qinshui County in Ze Prefecture, when people brought goods for official delivery he slightly raised the price paid for those items and lowered the assessed value of everything else.

sentences.zh: 官有所須，不強賦民，聽以所有與官為入，度相當則止，率常先辦。

translations.literal: When the government needed things, he did not force levies on the people; he allowed them to give what they had to the government as payment, stopping when equivalent value was reached, and usually fulfilled requirements ahead of schedule.
translations.idiomatic: When the government needed supplies, he never forced levies on the people. He let them contribute whatever they had until the required value was met, and he usually fulfilled quotas well ahead of deadline.

sentences.zh: 河外用兵，督餫轉西界，夕宿洪谷口。

translations.literal: When troops were deployed beyond the Yellow River, he supervised grain transport to the western frontier; one evening they camped at Honggu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign beyond the Yellow River he supervised grain transport to the western frontier. One evening the convoy camped at Honggu Pass.

sentences.zh: 仲元相其地，乃寇所由徑路，亟命去之。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan surveyed the place and saw it was a route used by bandits; he urgently ordered departure.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan surveyed the terrain and saw it lay on a bandit route. He immediately ordered the convoy to move on.

sentences.zh: 民以困乏為辭，不聽，寇果夜出劫諸部，沁水獨免。

translations.literal: The people pleaded exhaustion; he would not listen; bandits did indeed come out by night to raid various prefectures, and Qinshui alone was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The people pleaded exhaustion, but he would not listen. Bandits did raid neighboring prefectures that night, and Qinshui alone was spared.

sentences.zh: 後二十年，其子過縣，父老拜泣曰：「河西之役，非公無今日矣。」

translations.literal: Twenty years later, when his son passed through the county, village elders bowed and wept, saying: "In the campaign west of the River, had it not been for you, we would not be here today."
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years later, when his son passed through the county, the elders bowed and wept, saying, "Had it not been for your father in the campaign west of the River, we would not be alive today."

sentences.zh: 初，軍期尚緩，而仲元督行良急。

translations.literal: At first the army's deadline was still relaxed, but Zhongyuan pressed the transport very hard.
translations.idiomatic: At first the army's deadline was still lenient, but Zhongyuan drove the transport crews relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 至則芻糧有不集者皆可賤市，後期者物數倍其價，民始知其為利。

translations.literal: When they arrived, hay and grain that had not been collected could all be bought cheaply; those arriving late paid several times the price—the people then realized this had been to their benefit.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, uncollected fodder and grain could be bought at bargain prices, while latecomers paid several times as much. Only then did the people understand that his urgency had worked to their advantage.

sentences.zh: 州買羊，斂民差出錢帛滋蔓，病民為甚，仲元更其令，戶才費錢百。

translations.literal: The prefecture bought sheep; collecting corvée money and silk from the people spread endlessly and greatly harmed them. Zhongyuan changed the order—each household paid only a hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture's practice of buying sheep had spawned ever-growing corvée levies in cash and silk, crushing the people. Zhongyuan revised the order so that each household paid only a hundred cash.

sentences.zh: 又遣吏市羔於他所，明年以供州，不科一錢。

translations.literal: He also sent clerks to buy lambs elsewhere; the next year they would supply the prefecture—not levying a single cash.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent clerks to buy lambs elsewhere so that the following year the prefecture would be supplied without levying a single cash from the people.

sentences.zh: 徙知鄖鄉縣，宰相張士遜先塋隸境內，將屬之，召不往。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Yunxiang County; Grand Councilor Zhang Shisun's ancestral tomb fell within the district and was to be put under special jurisdiction—summoned, he would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Yunxiang County, he was summoned when Grand Councilor Zhang Shisun's ancestral tomb within the district was to be placed under special jurisdiction—but he refused to go.

sentences.zh: 至則按籍均役之，雖堂帖求免，不為減。

translations.literal: Once there, he assigned labor evenly according to the registers; even when official letters from the grand councilor's office sought exemption, he would not reduce it.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he assigned corvée labor evenly according to the registers. Even when letters from the grand councilor's office sought exemption, he would not reduce the assessment.

sentences.zh: 歷知光、虔、虢三州，官光祿卿，改中散大夫。
