translations.literal: He served in succession as prefect of Guang, Qian, and Guo Prefectures; reached the rank of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; and was changed to Grand Master for Miscellaneous Uses.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Guang, Qian, and Guo Prefectures, rose to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and was promoted to Grand Master for Miscellaneous Uses.

sentences.zh: 戒諸子曰：「吾入官五十年，未嘗以私怒加人，雖杖刑之微，苟有兩比，不敢與輕法，以是為報國耳。」

translations.literal: He admonished his sons: "In fifty years of office I have never let private anger fall on anyone—even for trivial bamboo punishment, if there are two sides to the dispute, I dare not apply the lightest penalty; that has been my way of repaying the state."
translations.idiomatic: He admonished his sons, "In fifty years of office I never let private anger dictate my judgments. Even for the lightest bamboo punishment, if both sides had a case, I never applied the lenient penalty. That is how I have served the state."

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 餘良肱

translations.literal: Yu Lianggong.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Lianggong.

sentences.zh: 餘良肱，字康臣，洪州分寧人。

translations.literal: Yu Lianggong, style name Kangchen, was a native of Fenning in Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Lianggong, courtesy name Kangchen, came from Fenning in Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調荊南司理參軍。

translations.literal: He attained the jinshi degree and was appointed judicial assistant in Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he was appointed judicial assistant in Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 屬縣捕得殺人者，既自誣服，良肱視驗屍與刃，疑之曰：「豈有刃盈尺傷不及寸乎？」

translations.literal: A subordinate county had captured a murderer who had already confessed. Lianggong examined the corpse and the blade and doubted, saying: "How could a blade a full foot long leave wounds less than an inch?"
translations.idiomatic: When a subordinate county captured a murderer who had already confessed, Lianggong examined the corpse and the weapon and grew suspicious. "How can a foot-long blade leave wounds less than an inch deep?" he asked.

sentences.zh: 白府請自捕逮，未幾，果獲真殺人者。

translations.literal: He reported to the prefecture and asked to capture and investigate himself; before long, the true killer was indeed caught.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to the prefectural office and asked to conduct the investigation himself. Before long the real killer was captured.

sentences.zh: 民有失財物逾十萬，逮平民數十人，方暑，搒掠號呼聞於外；

translations.literal: A resident lost property exceeding a hundred thousand; dozens of commoners were arrested; it was midsummer, and the sounds of flogging and cries could be heard outside;
translations.idiomatic: When a resident reported the loss of property worth more than a hundred thousand cash, dozens of commoners were arrested. It was midsummer, and the sounds of flogging and screaming could be heard outside;

sentences.zh: 或有附吏耳語，良肱陰知其為盜，亟捕詰之，贓盡得。

translations.literal: Some whispered to the clerks at his ear; Lianggong secretly knew these were the thieves; he quickly arrested and interrogated them, and all the stolen goods were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: some whispered in the clerks' ears. Lianggong secretly suspected they were the thieves, quickly arrested and interrogated them, and recovered all the stolen goods.

sentences.zh: 改大理寺丞，出知湘陰縣。

translations.literal: He was changed to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and went out to govern Xiangyin County.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and appointed magistrate of Xiangyin County.

sentences.zh: 縣逋米數千石，歲責里胥代輸，良肱論列之，遂蠲其籍。

translations.literal: The county owed several thousand shi of rice; every year village headmen were forced to pay in lieu. Lianggong presented the case and the obligation was struck from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: The county owed several thousand shi of rice, and each year village headmen were forced to pay on its behalf. Lianggong presented the case to higher authority and had the debt stricken from the registers.

sentences.zh: 通判杭州，江潮善溢，漂官民廬舍，良肱累石堤二十里障之，潮不為害。

translations.literal: As vice prefect of Hangzhou, the river tides often overflowed and swept away official and private dwellings; Lianggong built a stone dike twenty li long to block them, and the tides no longer caused harm.
translations.idiomatic: As vice prefect of Hangzhou, he faced tidal floods that regularly swept away public and private buildings. Lianggong built a stone dike twenty li long to hold the tides back, and the floods ceased to do harm.

sentences.zh: 時王陶為屬官，常以氣犯府帥，吏或訴陶，帥挾憾欲按之，良肱不可曰：「使陶以罪去，是以直不容也。」

translations.literal: At the time Wang Tao was a subordinate official who often offended the prefect by his temper; some clerks complained about Tao, and the prefect, harboring resentment, wanted to investigate him. Lianggong refused, saying: "If Tao were to leave in disgrace, it would mean that integrity is not tolerated."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Tao served as a subordinate official and often offended the prefect with his blunt manner. When some clerks complained, the prefect, nursing a grudge, wanted to bring charges against him. Lianggong objected: "If Tao were driven out on false charges, it would mean the upright man has no place here."

sentences.zh: 帥遂已。

translations.literal: The prefect then dropped the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 後陶官於朝，果以直聞。

translations.literal: Later Tao served at court and indeed became known for his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tao served at court and did indeed become renowned for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 知虔州，士大夫死嶺外者，喪車自虔出，多弱子寡婦。

translations.literal: Governing Qian Prefecture—when scholar-officials died beyond the Ling mountains, funeral processions departed from Qian; many were weak children and widows.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Qian Prefecture, he saw that when scholar-officials died beyond the Ling mountains, their funeral processions passed through Qian bearing many helpless children and widows.

sentences.zh: 良肱悉力振護，孤女無所依者，出俸錢嫁之。

translations.literal: Lianggong exerted all effort to support and protect them; orphan girls with nowhere to turn—he paid from his salary to marry them off.
translations.idiomatic: Lianggong did everything in his power to assist and protect them. Orphan girls with no one to rely on he married off at his own expense from his official salary.

sentences.zh: 以母老，得知南康軍。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old, he obtained the post of military prefect of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was elderly, he obtained the post of military prefect of Nankang so he could be nearer to her.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除，為三司使判官。

translations.literal: Upon completing mourning for his mother, he served as commissioner-assessor to the Commissioner of the Three Sections.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for his mother, he served as commissioner-assessor to the Commissioner of the Three Sections.

sentences.zh: 方關、陝用兵，朝議貸在京民錢，良肱力爭之，會大臣亦以為言，議遂格。

translations.literal: Just then campaigns were underway in Guan and Shaan; the court debated lending money from capital residents; Lianggong strongly opposed it; coincidentally high ministers also spoke against it, and the proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Just as campaigns were underway in Guan and Shaan, the court debated requisitioning loans from the capital's residents. Lianggong argued forcefully against it, and when senior ministers raised the same objection, the proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 內府出腐幣售三司，三司吏將受之，良肱獨曰：「若賦諸軍，軍且怨；

translations.literal: The inner treasury put out rotten currency to sell to the Three Sections; the Three Sections clerks were about to accept it. Lianggong alone said: "If it is distributed to the armies, the troops will resent it;
translations.idiomatic: When the inner treasury offered degraded currency for sale to the Three Sections and the clerks were about to accept it, Lianggong alone objected: "If this is distributed to the armies, the soldiers will resent it;

sentences.zh: 不則貨諸民，民且病。

translations.literal: Otherwise, if sold to the people, the people will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: and if it is sold to the people instead, the people will be ruined.

sentences.zh: 請付文思，以奉帷幄。

translations.literal: I ask that it be sent to the Department of Culture and Ideas to supply the imperial bedding and curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Send it to the Department of Imperial Manufactures to supply the palace furnishings.

sentences.zh: 改知明州。

translations.literal: He was changed to govern Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方治汴渠，留提舉汴河司。

translations.literal: The court was then working on the Bian Canal; he was retained as director of the Bian River Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: While the court was repairing the Bian Canal, he was retained as director of the Bian River Bureau.

sentences.zh: 汴水澱汙，流且緩，執政主狹河議。

translations.literal: The Bian River was silted and polluted, its flow slowing; those in power favored the narrow-river plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian River was choked with silt and its current sluggish. Those in power favored a plan to narrow the channel.

sentences.zh: 良肱謂：「善治水者不與水爭地。

translations.literal: Lianggong said: "One who excels at managing water does not compete with water for land.
translations.idiomatic: Lianggong argued, "A master of water management does not fight the river for land.

sentences.zh: 方冬水涸，宜自京左浚治，以及畿右，三年，可使水復行地中。」

translations.literal: Now in winter the water is low; one ought to dredge from the left of the capital eastward through the right of the capital precinct—within three years the water can be made to run in its channel again."
translations.idiomatic: Now, while winter has drawn the water down, we should dredge from east of the capital through the capital precinct. In three years the river can be made to run in its proper channel again."

sentences.zh: 弗聽。

translations.literal: They would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: They would not listen.

sentences.zh: 又議伐汴堤木以資狹河。

translations.literal: They also proposed cutting the trees on the Bian dikes to fund the narrow-river project.
translations.idiomatic: They also proposed felling the trees along the Bian dikes to finance the channel-narrowing project.

sentences.zh: 良肱言：「自泗至京千餘里，江、淮漕卒接踵，暑行多病暍，藉蔭以休。

translations.literal: Lianggong said: "From Si to the capital is more than a thousand li; grain-transport crews from the Jiang and Huai follow one after another—in summer travel many suffer heatstroke; they rely on shade to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Lianggong objected: "From Si to the capital is more than a thousand li. Grain-transport crews from the Yangzi and Huai regions follow one after another. In summer many succumb to heatstroke and depend on this shade to rest.

sentences.zh: 又其根盤錯，與堤為固，伐之不便。」

translations.literal: Moreover their roots are tangled and interlocked, binding the dike firm—cutting them would be inadvisable."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, their roots are tangled and interlocked with the dike, holding it firm—felling them would be unwise."

sentences.zh: 屢爭不能得，乃請不與其事。

translations.literal: He repeatedly contested but could not prevail, and then requested not to participate in the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He argued repeatedly but could not prevail, and finally asked to be excused from the project altogether.

sentences.zh: 執政雖怒，竟不為屈。

translations.literal: Those in power were angry but in the end he did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power were furious, but in the end he would not bend.

sentences.zh: 改太常少卿、知潤州，遷光祿卿、知宣州，治為江東最。

translations.literal: He was changed to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and governor of Run Prefecture; was promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and governor of Xuan Prefecture—his governance ranked first in Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Run Prefecture, then promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and prefect of Xuan Prefecture, where his administration ranked first in Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 請老，提舉洪州玉隆觀，卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: He requested retirement; was appointed director of the Yulong Abbey in Hong Prefecture; and died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement and was appointed director of the Yulong Abbey in Hong Prefecture. He died at eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 七子，卞、爽最知名。

translations.literal: He had seven sons; Bian and Shuang were the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons; Bian and Shuang were the best known.

sentences.zh: 卞，字洪範；

translations.literal: Bian, style name Hongfan;
translations.idiomatic: Bian, courtesy name Hongfan;

sentences.zh: 爽，字荀龍，皆以任子恩試校書郎。

translations.literal: Shuang, style name Xunlong—both entered the proofreader office by the privilege of sons of officials taking the examination.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang, courtesy name Xunlong—both entered the proofreader office through the privilege granted to sons of officials.

sentences.zh: 卞博學多大略，累為唐州判官、湖北安撫司勾當機宜文字。

translations.literal: Bian was broadly learned and possessed great strategic vision; he served repeatedly as vice prefect of Tang Prefecture and chief clerk for policy documentation in the Hubei Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was widely learned and possessed great strategic vision. He served repeatedly as vice prefect of Tang Prefecture and as chief policy clerk in the Hubei Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 討叛蠻有功，知沅州。

translations.literal: For merits in suppressing rebellious barbarians, he governed Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements in suppressing rebellious tribes, he was appointed prefect of Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蠻殺沿邊巡檢，卞設方略復平之，加奉議郎。

translations.literal: When barbarians killed a frontier patrol inspector, Bian devised a strategy and pacified them again; he was promoted to Gentleman for Fostering Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When tribesmen killed a frontier patrol inspector, Bian devised a strategy and restored order. He was promoted to Gentleman for Fostering Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 先是，良肱為鼎州推官，五溪蠻叛，良肱運糧境上，周知其利害，上書言：「此彈丸地，不足煩朝廷費，不如棄與而就撫之。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Lianggong was judicial assistant in Ding Prefecture, the Five Streams tribes rebelled. Lianggong transported grain to the border, learned thoroughly the advantages and harms, and memorialized: "This is a pellet-sized territory, not worth troubling the court's expense; better to abandon it and then pacify them through appeasement."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Lianggong was judicial assistant in Ding Prefecture, the Five Streams tribes rebelled. He transported grain to the frontier, studied the terrain and its risks in detail, and memorialized: "This is a tiny territory not worth the court's expense. Better to withdraw and win them over by appeasement."

sentences.zh: 當時是其議，未果棄也。

translations.literal: At the time people approved his proposal, but abandoning the region was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: His proposal won approval at the time, but the withdrawal was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 及蠻叛，斷渠陽道，扼官軍不得進，卞適使湖北，帥唐義問即授卞節制諸將。

translations.literal: When the tribes rebelled they cut the Qianyang route and blocked government troops from advancing; Bian happened to be on mission in Hubei, and the commander Tang Yiwen immediately gave him authority over all generals.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes rebelled they severed the Qianyang route and blocked the government armies. Bian happened to be on assignment in Hubei, and the commander Tang Yiwen immediately placed all generals under his command.

sentences.zh: 陰選死士三千人，夜銜枚繞出賊背，伐山開道，漏未盡數刻，入渠陽。

translations.literal: Secretly he selected three thousand dare-to-die troops who at night took sticks in their mouths, circled behind the rebels, cut through the mountains to open a path, and before the night watch ended had entered Qianyang.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly chose three thousand elite troops who, at night with gag-sticks in their mouths, circled behind the enemy, cut a path through the mountains, and reached Qianyang within a few hours before dawn.

sentences.zh: 黎明整眾出，賊大駭，盡銳來戰，奮擊大破之。

translations.literal: At dawn he marshaled his forces and sallied forth; the rebels were greatly alarmed, brought their full strength to battle, and were fiercely struck and utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he formed his troops and marched out. The rebels were terrified, threw their full strength into battle, and were smashed in a fierce assault.

sentences.zh: 鼓行度險，賊七遇七敗，斬首數千級，蠻遂降。

translations.literal: Beating drums they advanced through the difficult terrain; seven times they met the enemy and seven times defeated them, beheading several thousand, and the tribes then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Beating drums, they pressed through the difficult terrain. Seven times they met the enemy and seven times routed them, taking several thousand heads, until the tribes surrendered.

sentences.zh: 尋有詔廢渠陽軍為砦，盡拔居人護出之。

translations.literal: Soon an edict abolished Qianyang Army as a garrison and made it a stockade, evacuating all inhabitants under escort.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict downgraded Qianyang Army to a stockade and ordered all inhabitants evacuated under escort.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，治棄渠陽罪，免歸。

translations.literal: Early in the Shaosheng era he was prosecuted for abandoning Qianyang, dismissed, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaosheng era he was punished for the abandonment of Qianyang, dismissed from office, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，復奉議郎，管勾玉隆觀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne he was restored as Gentleman for Discussion and assigned to manage Yulong Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong took the throne he was restored to Gentleman for Discussion and assigned to manage Yulong Abbey.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復渠陽為靖州，又論前事免，終於家。

translations.literal: Before long Qianyang was restored as Jing Prefecture; he was again prosecuted over the earlier affair and dismissed, dying at home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Qianyang was restored as Jing Prefecture. He was again prosecuted over the earlier affair, dismissed, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 爽尚氣自信，不少貶以合世。

translations.literal: Shuang was high-spirited and self-confident, seldom lowering himself to conform to the world.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang was proud and self-assured, rarely bending himself to suit the times.

sentences.zh: 應元豐詔，上便宜十五事，言過剴切。

translations.literal: Responding to the Yuanfeng edict he submitted fifteen expedient proposals, his words excessively sharp and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: In response to the Yuanfeng edict he submitted fifteen policy proposals, his language excessively sharp and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 元祐末，爽復極言請太皇太后還政事，章惇憾爽不附己，乃擿其言為謗訕，以瀛州防禦推官除名，竄封州。

translations.literal: Late in the Yuanyou era Shuang again spoke forcefully asking the Grand Empress Dowager to return governmental affairs; Zhang Dun resented that Shuang would not attach himself to him and seized on his words as slander, stripping him of rank as judicial assistant under the defense commissioner of Ying Prefecture and banishing him to Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yuanyou era Shuang again urged forcefully that the Grand Empress Dowager return governmental power. Zhang Dun, resenting Shuang's refusal to side with him, seized on his words as slander, stripped him of rank, and banished him to Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久之，起知明州，未行，以言者罷，監東嶽廟。

translations.literal: After a long time he was raised to govern Ming Prefecture; before he departed, critics had him dismissed and made him supervisor of the Eastern Peak Temple.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was appointed prefect of Ming Prefecture, but before he could take up the post critics had him removed and made supervisor of the Eastern Peak Temple.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中，與卞俱入黨籍。

translations.literal: In the Chongning era he and Bian were both entered on the faction register.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongning era he and Bian were both entered on the proscribed faction register.

sentences.zh: 潘夙，字伯恭，鄭王美從孫也。

translations.literal: Pan Su, style name Bogong, was a collateral descendant of Prince Mei of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Su, courtesy name Bogong, was a collateral descendant of Prince Mei of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，上書論時政，授仁壽主簿。

translations.literal: In the Tiansheng era he memorialized on current affairs and was appointed chief clerk of Renshou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiansheng era he submitted a memorial on current affairs and was appointed chief clerk of Renshou.

sentences.zh: 久之，知韶州，擢江西轉運判官，提點廣西、湖北刑獄。

translations.literal: After a long time he was prefect of Shao Prefecture, promoted to transport commissioner-assessor of Jiangxi, and intendant of penal affairs for Guangxi and Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he became prefect of Shao Prefecture, was promoted to transport commissioner-assessor of Jiangxi, and served as intendant of penal affairs for Guangxi and Hubei.

sentences.zh: 邵州蠻叛，湖南騷動，遷轉運使，專制蠻事，親督兵破其團峒九十。

translations.literal: When the tribes of Shao Prefecture rebelled and Hunan was in turmoil, he was transferred to transport commissioner with sole authority over tribal affairs, personally directing troops to break ninety stockaded settlements.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes of Shao Prefecture rebelled and Hunan was thrown into turmoil, he was made transport commissioner with sole authority over tribal affairs and personally led troops to destroy ninety stockaded settlements.

sentences.zh: 徙知滑州，改湖北轉運便，知桂州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Hua Prefecture, changed to Hubei transport commissioner, and made prefect of Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hua Prefecture, then made Hubei transport commissioner and prefect of Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坐在湖北時匿名書誣判官韓繹，謫監隨州酒稅。

translations.literal: He was convicted because while in Hubei he had written an anonymous letter slandering commissioner-assessor Han Yi and was demoted to supervise the wine tax of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was convicted of writing an anonymous letter while in Hubei slandering commissioner-assessor Han Yi and was demoted to supervise the wine tax of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 起知光化軍。

translations.literal: He was raised to govern Guanghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored and appointed military prefect of Guanghua.

sentences.zh: 大臣以將帥才舉之，易端州刺史，再遷徙鄜州。

translations.literal: High ministers recommended him for talent as a general and he was moved to prefect of Duan Prefecture, then transferred again to Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers recommended him as a commander, and he was moved to Duan Prefecture, then transferred again to Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召對，訪交、廣事稱旨，還司封郎中、直昭文館，復知桂州。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience, his answers on Jiaozhi and Guang affairs pleased the emperor; he returned as bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, Hanlin attendant at the Zhaowen Pavilion, and again prefect of Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience, his answers on affairs in Jiaozhi and Guangdong pleased the emperor. He was made bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, Hanlin attendant at the Zhaowen Pavilion, and again prefect of Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 交人敗於占城，偽表稱賀以為大捷，神宗詔之曰：「智高之難方二十年，中人之情，燕安忽事，直謂山僻蠻獠，無可慮之理。

translations.literal: The people of Jiaozhi were defeated by Champa and sent a false memorial of congratulation claiming a great victory; Emperor Shenzong admonished him: "The trouble of Nong Zhigao was only twenty years ago. The temper of middling men is to dwell in ease and neglect affairs, simply assuming that remote mountain barbarians have no cause for concern.
translations.idiomatic: After the people of Jiaozhi were defeated by Champa they sent a false memorial of congratulation claiming a great victory. Emperor Shenzong admonished him: "Nong Zhigao's rebellion was only twenty years ago. Ordinary men grow complacent in comfort and neglect danger, assuming that remote mountain tribes can never threaten us.

sentences.zh: 殊不思禍生於所忽，唐六詔為中國患，此前事之師也。

translations.literal: They give no thought that disaster arises from what is overlooked; the Six Zhao of Tang were a scourge to China—this is a teacher from events past.
translations.idiomatic: They forget that disaster grows from neglect. The Six Zhao of Tang were a scourge to China—that lesson should still be before us.

sentences.zh: 卿本將家子，寄要蕃，宜體朕意，悉心經度。」

translations.literal: You are by origin a general's son, entrusted with a key frontier post; you should embody my intent and devote yourself wholeheartedly to planning."
translations.idiomatic: You come from a military family and hold a critical frontier post. Embody my intent and devote yourself wholeheartedly to planning."

sentences.zh: 夙遂上書陳交阯可取狀，且將發兵。

translations.literal: Su then memorialized setting forth how Jiaozhi could be taken and was about to mobilize troops.
translations.idiomatic: Su then memorialized on how Jiaozhi could be conquered and was about to mobilize troops.

sentences.zh: 未報，而徙河北轉運使，歷度支、鹽鐵副使，知河中府。

translations.literal: Before a reply came he was transferred to Hebei transport commissioner, served successively as vice commissioner of revenue and of salt and iron, and was prefect of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Before any reply arrived he was transferred to Hebei transport commissioner, served as vice commissioner of revenue and of salt and iron, and became prefect of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 章惇察訪荊湖，討南、北江蠻徭，陳夙憂邊狀，以知潭州。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun inspected Jinghu and Hunan, campaigning against the southern and northern river Man and Yao; Su reported anxieties about the frontier and was made prefect of Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dun inspected Jinghu and Hunan and campaigned against the southern and northern river tribes, Su reported his concerns about the frontier and was appointed prefect of Tan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 再遷光祿卿，知荊南、鄂州，卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, governed Jingnan and E Prefectures, and died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, governed Jingnan and E Prefectures, and died at seventy.

sentences.zh: 論曰：士之官斯世，有一善可稱，致生民咸被其澤於無窮者，故州郡之寄為尤重，張田免禁兵毒於瘴厲，士宏考圭田出於實輸，朱景父子、諲、載、煦、渙、士宏、壽隆輩，皆有德在民。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: When scholars serve in this age, if they have one virtue that can be praised and cause the people to receive their benefit without end, then the charge of prefectures and districts is especially weighty. Zhang Tian spared forbidden troops from miasmic poison; Lu Shihong audited gui fields against actual payments; Zhu Jing father and son, Rong Yin, Li Zai, Dan Xu, Yao Huan, Lu Shihong, Zhu Shoulong, and their like all had virtue among the people.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: When men of learning serve in public office, even a single virtue worth praising can bring lasting benefit to the people. For this reason prefectural posts carry special weight. Zhang Tian spared forbidden troops from malarial poison; Lu Shihong audited noble estates against actual tax payments; Zhu Jing and his son, Rong Yin, Li Zai, Dan Xu, Yao Huan, Lu Shihong, Zhu Shoulong, and others like them all left virtue among the people.

sentences.zh: 仲元不以私怒加人，良肱明於折獄，夙以將家子而能留心邊務，用當其材，舉能其官。

translations.literal: Yang Zhongyuan did not visit private anger on others; Lianggong was clear in deciding cases; Su, though a general's son, could attend to frontier affairs—when employed according to their talents, each fulfilled his office.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhongyuan did not let private anger govern his judgments; Lianggong was skilled at deciding cases; Su, though born to a military family, gave serious attention to frontier affairs. When each was used according to his talent, all fulfilled their offices well.

sentences.zh: 若琮也雖長於吏治，而所至掊克，君子奚取焉。

translations.literal: As for Cong, though skilled in administrative governance, wherever he went he extorted and squeezed—what would a gentleman approve in that?
translations.idiomatic: As for Cong, though skilled in administration, wherever he went he extorted the people—what gentleman would approve of that?
